event.title: Blind Boys of Alabama Present Songs In the Key of Life
event.description:
“always hunting for – and finding – the perfect note or harmony that lifts an old tune into the sublime” – Time

 

Six-Time Grammy Winners
Gospel Music Hall of Fame Inductees

The legendary Blind Boys of Alabama bring their transcendent harmonies and spiritual power. Here, they celebrate the fiftieth anniversary of Stevie Wonder’s iconic album Songs in the Key of Life. This special presentation pairs many of Stevie Wonder’s classic songs with beloved selections from the Blind Boys’ own celebrated repertoire. Moreover, they blend gospel, soul, and Americana in a joyful performance that honors both musical legacies.

Now, the Blind Boys have lifted spirits and moved souls for over seventy-five years. Furthermore, they continue their mission of spreading light and love through the universal language of music. In 2003, the Blind Boys earned a Grammy Award for an album that included their acclaimed cover of Stevie Wonder’s “Higher Ground.” Further, this version later featured in film and television, including FX’s Fargo. In 2007, Stevie Wonder presented Blind Boys singer Jimmy Carter with a Vision Award for Lifetime Achievement. Thus, this underscores their enduring impact on music and culture.

Here, this show features classics like: “Sir Duke,” “I Wish,” “As,” and more.

Recommended for fans of Mavis Staples, The Holmes Brothers, Stevie Wonder and Taj Mahal.

📸: Cole Weber

event.title: Alison Brown
event.description:
“Brown’s banjo is an instrument possessed of a unique sonic signature and an inescapable beauty” – Billboard

 

One of the most multi-faceted minds in roots music, Alison Brown is a Grammy-winning musician and a Grammy-nominated producer. Additionally, she is a former investment banker (with an AB from Harvard and an MBA from UCLA). Also, she co-founded The Compass Records Group which celebrated its thirtieth anniversary in 2023.

Alison began her musical career as a teenager in the Southern California bluegrass scene. Now, she has built a reputation as one of today’s most forward-thinking and innovative banjo players. She is known for taking the instrument far beyond its Appalachian roots by blending bluegrass and jazz influences into a sonic tapestry. Thus, she has earned praise and recognition from a variety of national tastemakers. For example, The Wall Street Journal, CBS Sunday Morning, NPR, and USA Today.

Steve Martin and Alison Brown released their debut collaborative album, Safe, Sensible and Sane, in 2025. There, it features guest appearances from Jackson Browne, Vince Gill, the Indigo Girls, Tim O’Brien, Jason Mraz, Della Mae, and more. Moreover, Safe, Sensible and Sane emerges as a captivating new turn in the evolution of banjo music.

There, the album follows their chart-topping collaborations “Foggy Morning Breaking”, “Bluegrass Radio”, and “Wall Guitar (Since You Said Goodbye)”. Here, these longtime friends and banjo aficionados have crafted a collection of banjo-inspired songs. Further, they are built on Brown’s daringly inventive melodies and Martin’s idiosyncratic yet ineffably tender lyrics. 

Recommended for fans of Steep Canyon Rangers, Yonder Mountain String Band, Della Mae and Béla Fleck.

event.title: John Scofield’s Electrospective
event.description:
“Scofield is one of the most prolific and admired jazz musicians of his generation” – NPR

 

Through his fifty-four-year career, three-time Grammy Award winner John Scofield has occasionally detoured from the traditions of straight-ahead jazz. There, he explores a blend of funk and jazz that has led to some of his most popular projects. In 2026, Scofield looks back at many of his now classic fusion groove compositions with Electrospective. 

Not intending to replicate earlier fan favorites, he plans instead to revisit them with the seasoned perspective of several decades. Here, he culls tunes from his Blue Matter, Uberjam, and AGoGo bands, each responsible for a few recordings. Additionally, he will play new material in the same vein. 

Moreover, Scofield looks forward to teaming up with a stellar band of colleagues. Electrospective will rely on interpretative input from Scofield alum and super funk drummer/producer Adam Deitch (Lettuce). Also, multidimensional Larry Goldings (Scary Goldings, James Taylor) on keyboards. Additionally, legendary bassist Oteil Burbridge (Dead & Co., Tedeschi Trucks, Allman Brothers). With this repertoire so frequently (and loudly) requested by audience members, Scofield is glad to have a band that will truly do the music justice.

Recommended for fans of Pat Metheny, Lettuce, Karl Denson’s Tiny Universe and Medeski, Martin & Wood.

event.title: An Evening with Lucinda Williams & Her Band: World’s Gone Wrong Tour
event.description:
Acoustic Shows with Lucinda Williams & Her Band:
Blues, Ballads & More: A Quiet Night with Lucinda Williams & Her Band
NOV 16 • 7:00pm Performance

Blues, Ballads & More: A Quiet Night with Lucinda Williams & Her Band
NOV 17 • 7:00pm Performance

“perfect… clearly in a league of her own” – Chicago Reader

 

“My dad, as a poet, always told me to never censor myself – that’s one of his cardinal rules of creative writing,” says multiple-Grammy-winning singer-songwriter Lucinda Williams. “That became my motto which I’ve stuck by all these years.” Miller Williams’ advice clearly is borne out on Lucinda’s powerful eighteenth studio album, 2026’s provocative World’s Gone Wrong. “I felt a sense of urgency in making this record,” she adds.

Filled with gut-wrenching topical songs, the album’s ten tracks were written and recorded in a blast of collaborative creativity. There, Lucinda and her co-writers ­– primarily husband/manager/co-producer Tom Overby and guitarist Doug Pettibone – grappled with the events of spring 2025. Moreover, a whole other album had been in the works. However, the “urgency” to address our current cataclysmic situation motivated Lucinda and company to cut World’s Gone Wrong in direct response. “Music is a powerful weapon,” she points out. “I want this record to make people aware, wake them up. I like to push people’s buttons.”

And that’s what Lucinda fans have come to depend on over the past forty-five years. Her back catalog boasts remarkable albums, including 1998’s game-changing Car Wheels on a Gravel Road. Additionally, she’s earned three Grammy awards and countless accolades, including Time Magazine naming her America’s Best Songwriter in 2001. Here, Williams is one of our most revered artists, beloved for her singular vocals and extraordinary songs. And in these troubling times, we need the light she shines on World’s Gone Wrong more than ever before.

Recommended for fans of Emmylou Harris, Gillian Welch, Steve Earle & Bob Dylan.

📸: Mark Seliger

event.title: Charles Lloyd Quartet
event.description:
“Charles Lloyd is an international treasure.” Carlos Santana

 

Charles Lloyd and Bill Frisell first joined forces in 2013 for a special project in Montreal. There, their connection was immediate and the joy of making music together endures. Over the years that followed, Bill toured and recorded with Charles in various formations; duo, trio, quartet and quintet. Additionally, their recordings together include I Long to See You, Tone Poem, and Chapel Trio. For his return to the Dakota, Charles has assembled a dream quartet. Here, renowned bassist Larry Grenadier joins the band, who was first heard with Charles on The Water Is Wide. Also, the rising young star on drums, Kweku Sumbry. 

“He’s expansive in his musical discourse yet without a wasted note.” – Wall Street Journal

“Ageless wonder Charles Lloyd is as dynamic as ever.” – Music in Minnesota

NEA Jazz Master Charles Lloyd, now in his eighth decade, has never sounded better. Voted Downbeat’s Jazzman of the Year in 1967, Lloyd was again voted the 2023 Artist of the Year. The arc of his contribution to this artform starts in the early 1960s, and the depth of his expression reflects a lifetime of experience.

“His shows, full of momentum and intuition, perfectly represent the idea that the best jazz needs to be experienced live.” – The New York Times

Over nearly five decades, Lloyd’s compositions have punctuated the post-bop period. He infused the traditional music with a host of world cultures and avant-garde improvisation.  “Lloyd is one of the greats, rather like Joan Miro in modern art, he has no peer save himself. Music of total transport and delight.” Jazzwise

Recommended for fans of John Coltrane, Abdullah Ibrahim, Dexter Gordon and Jason Moran.

event.title: Lee Roy Parnell w/ Special Guest Goldpine
event.description:
“All Lee Roy Parnell does is write great songs” – Pop Matters

 

No Depression may have said it best when they called Lee Roy Parnell “a fine writer blessed with a rich, soulful vocal delivery and a blistering array of guitar chops drawn almost equally from Texas blues, Memphis soul, and Southern rock traditions.”

Parnell is part of a long line of Texas roots-music eclectics. However, he is among the elite few who can be identified as a triple threat. First, he’s an ace guitarist who is known as one of the best slide guitarists on the planet. Also, his music includes blue-eyed soul, Delta blues, roadhouse rock, Southern boogie, Texas swing, country and gospel. Parnell draws from a broad range of musical sources and combines them with seamless dexterity. Also, unlike many other hard-to-pigeonhole artists, Parnell has enjoyed a run of success on the country and blues charts.

After honing his skills over more than a decade of playing clubs, Parnell laid a new foundation in Nashville. Then, upon earning a regular spot at the famed Bluebird Café and a publishing contract, Parnell launched his solo career. There, he scored many country hits including “A Little Bit Of You” (Number One hit). Also, “What Kind of Fools Do You Think I Am” & “Tender Moment” (both Number Two hits). Additionally, four other Top Ten hits: “Love Without Mercy”, “On The Road”, “I’m Holding My Own”, and “Heart’s Desire”. Further, Parnell has earned two Grammy nominations for his instrumental tracks.

Goldpine: bold + gold harmonies straight from Nashville. Winner of the Rocky Mountain Songwriter Contest and seen on NPR’s Mountain Stage. Their brand of “aggressive Americana” is a flawless channel for their bold and reminiscent compositions. Husband and wife of sixteen years, Goldpine just released their third album, appropriately titled Three.

Recommended for fans of Rodney Crowell, Rosanne Cash, Marty Stuart and Kathy Mattea.

“R&B-inflected saxophone… lyrical and intimate” – Jazz Times

 

Boney James is three decades into a career built on deep groove, melodic instinct and an unmistakably singular saxophone voice. However, James is still finding new ground. On 2026’s A Simple Man, his milestone twentieth studio album, the multi-platinum saxophonist delivers one of his most personal records.

James’ catalog has generated more than two billion on-demand streams in the United States. His honors include four Grammy nominations, three NAACP Image Award nominations, four RIAA Gold-certified records and a Soul Train Award. Also, Billboard named him one of the Top Three Contemporary Jazz Artists of the 2000s. Additionally, in 2024 he became the first artist to score twenty Number One singles on the Billboard Smooth Jazz chart. Further, recent collaborations have also earned him two Top Ten hits at Adult R&B.

For James, A Simple Man reflects a growing desire to strip away distraction and focus on what matters most. “As I’ve gotten older, I’ve realized I don’t need a lot to make me happy,”he says. “I love making music and playing my saxophone.”

Here, that clarity runs through the new album. Grammy-winning vocalist Ledisi, acclaimed trumpeter Marquis Hill, and legendary guitarist Larry Carlton all make guest appearances.

James’ R&B foundation runs deep. He turned professional at nineteen, spending his formative years touring with Morris Day, The Isley Brothers, Teena Marie and others. Then, James stepped forward with his 1992 debut, Trust. Further, more than three decades later, he remains focused not on preserving a legacy, but on continuing to grow.

And that may be the clearest expression of A Simple Man. Here, James is an artist who, after more than three decades, knows more clearly than ever what matters.

Recommended for fans of Rick Braun, Brian Culbertson, Kirk Whalum and Jeffrey Osborne.

“originality, intimacy, and volcanic expressiveness” – Boston Globe

 

Rickie Lee Jones is an American musician, storyteller, two-time Grammy winner and eight-time nominee. Moreover, The New Yorker named her the “premiere song-stylist and songwriter of her generation”. Also, Time magazine called her “The Duchess of Coolsville”.

Jones released her Grammy-nominated album Pieces of Treasure in 2023, a reunion with Russ Titelman. There, Russ produced her first two records. Additionally, Jones’ celebrated 2021 memoir Last Chance Texaco was named Book of the Year by MOJO. Then, it made Best of Year lists by NPR, Pitchfork, and many more. The Independent writes, “There has always been something defiant about Rickie Lee Jones… a voice from a dream, elusive yet familiar, transcendent, a messenger from another place.”

Recommended for fans of Joni Mitchell, Edie Brickell, Randy Newman and The Lounge Lizards.

event.title: Rachael & Vilray
event.description:
“tunes that echo the feel of standards, without dipping into a single musical or lyrical cliché.” – Downbeat

 

Brooklyn-based duo Rachael & Vilray have achieved a certain timeless quality with their singular take on traditional pop. There, they have accomplished this since their 2015 formation. Rooted in the language of an earlier age, their songs transcend nostalgia with wit and a flair for the theatrical. On their third album, 2025’s West of Broadway, vocalist Rachael Price (also of Lake Street Dive) and guitarist/singer/songwriter Vilray evolve. Moreover, they shed their music’s previous dreaminess to achieve a refreshing angularity built on left-of-center instrumentation. For example, vibraphone and alto saxophone coast above the moody strains of baritone sax and trombone. Thus, West of Broadway unfolds in a series of sharply drawn vignettes inspired by a recent fascination with classic musicals. Here, they bring their luminous vocals to offbeat tales of love and heartache along city streets.

Furthermore, West of Broadway took shape with renowned musicians like saxophonist Steve Wilson (formerly of Chick Corea’s Origin sextet). Additionally, drummer John Riley (Miles Davis, Dizzy Gillespie). Over the course of ten lush and effervescent tracks, the album delivers standouts like “Love Comes Around”. Here, this joyously romantic piece set the direction for the LP’s West Coast jazz-inspired aesthetic. Also, “My Key to Gramercy Park”, a fantastically salty number narrated by a well-to-do character. They live in lonely suspicion of all those who covet their key to the notoriously exclusive private park. Further, “Off Broadway”, where golden-voiced comedian Stephen Colbert joins in for what the duo dubs an “oddly grumpy anti-Broadway screed”. The album comes to life in the colorful detail and extravagant personality of Rachael & Vilray’s storytelling. West of Broadway ultimately immerses the audience in an exquisitely out-of-time vision of their beloved New York City.

Recommended for fans of Madeleine Peyroux, Stella Cole, Cyrille Aimée and Lake Street Dive.

event.title: The Beautiful Day: Kurt Elling Sings Christmas
event.description:
“the standout male vocalist of our time” – New York Times

 

Two-time Grammy winner and seventeen-time nominee Kurt Elling has secured his place among the world’s foremost jazz vocalists. There, he is renowned for his singular combination of robust swing, extraordinary musicianship and poetic insight. Furthermore, he was declared “the standout male vocalist of our time” by The New York Times. Elling’s career has been marked by decades of critical acclaim and an unprecedented fourteen-year run atop the DownBeat Critics Poll. Most recently, Elling brought his unmistakable voice and commanding stage presence to Broadway. There, he made his Broadway debut as Hermes in the Tony Award-winning musical Hadestown.

For the holiday season, Elling returns to the music of The Beautiful Day: Kurt Elling Sings Christmas. Here, this is his distinctive and deeply personal celebration of Christmas. Inventive, warm and full of surprises, The Beautiful Day reimagines the sounds of the season. Additionally, he combines traditional carols in fresh arrangements with unexpected songs and rediscovered treasures. At its heart are the universal themes of hope, light, wonder, mystery and goodwill that have always defined Elling’s approach to the holidays.

“I knew I didn’t want to make a ‘religious’ record, just as I knew I didn’t want to make a standard, swingin’ jazzy Christmas,” Elling has said. “I’m trying to expand my consciousness and embrace the goodness of the season, and I want to include everybody. For me, Christmas is a time of consideration, of pondering mysteries.”

Then, he brings that spirit to the stage. Kurt Elling’s holiday concerts offer an evening that is at once joyful, searching, soulful and unmistakably his own. Here, experience a contemporary celebration of the season from one of today’s most acclaimed and adventurous vocal artists.

Recommended for fans of Frank Sinatra, Gregory Porter, John Pizzarelli and Cyrille Aimée.

📸: Elliot Mandel

event.title: Turn Turn Turn
event.description:
“Gorgeous harmonies and beautiful finger-picking” – Americana UK

 

Turn Turn Turn bonded over their mutual love of close harmony 60s and 70s country, folk, and pop music. Then, they formed an original Americana band. To create their distinctive sound, the band “turns” to the distant past of early American recorded music. Then, they “turn” again to that renaissance of the 1960s and 1970s. Finally, they “turn” again to the present looking forward. 

Members Adam Levy (guitar, vocals) and Barb Brynstad (bass, vocals) are mainstays of the Minnesota music scene. Together, they craft an infectious, pop-infused Americana. Even though Turn Turn Turn was born as a cover band, the group’s original material – sweetheart alt-country folk-pop – quickly stole the spotlight. Here, their Laurel Canyon meets 70s-Nashville-cosmic soul vibe is layered with three-part harmonies that stitch the band’s musical tapestry together.

Adam Levy is a veteran of the Minnesota rock scene, best known for leading up the alt-rock band The Honeydogs. As a prolific songwriter and producer, he has worked across many genres and performed worldwide. Joe Henry called Levy’s solo album Naubinway “love in action. A courageous and generous offering, where ghosts abound, facing the quiet inevitable that forever walks with us. It’s a record with soul and deep compassion. It is a beautiful and remarkable piece of work.”

Barb Brynstad is an in-demand musician with decades-long roots in the Twin Cities music community. As a singer, bassist, and guitarist, she has performed with various musicians, including Chastity Brown (folk/Americana). Also, Tina Schlieske (pop/rock), Willie Wisely (pop/rock), and the late great Willie Murphy (blues/soul).

Recommended for fans of Tina Schlieske, Eilen Jewell, The Cactus Blossoms and Margo Price.

“a star with megawatt energy and a breathtaking breadth of talent” – Theater Pizzazz

 

Swedish musical sensation Gunhild Carling is an internationally acclaimed superstar whose show is a can’t-miss event! Whether she’s singing favorite swinging jazz standards, playing one of many instruments (trumpet, trombone, harmonica, oboe, harp, flute, recorder or jazz bagpipe!) or juggling and tap dancing, Gunhild’s sublime showmanship shines. event.title: Leo Kottke: Live at The Ordway
event.description:
“wild, highly technical blend of bluegrass, folk, and jazz and classical” – Rolling Stone

 

Prolific guitarist Leo Kottke boasts an impressive body of work and an unrivaled fingerpicking style. His forty-plus albums over four decades have earned him two Grammy nominations and widespread acclaim. Drawing inspiration from folk, blues and jazz, he plays his signature six-string and twelve-string guitars with effortless aptitude, a big heart and an even bigger grin. 

Kottke was born in Athens, Georgia, but left town after a year and a half. Raised in twelve different states, he absorbed a variety of musical influences as a child. There, he flirted with both violin and trombone, before abandoning Stravinsky for the guitar at age eleven.

He added a love for the country blues of Mississippi John Hurt to the music of John Philip Sousa and Preston Epps. Then, Kottke joined the Navy underage, to be underwater, and eventually lost some hearing shooting at lightbulbs in the Atlantic. He served on the USS Halfbeak, a diesel submarine.

Discharged in 1964, he settled in the Twin Cities area and became a fixture at Minneapolis’ Scholar Coffeehouse. Further, this venue had been home to Bob Dylan and John Koerner.

Kottke has been awarded two Grammy nominations. Also, a Doctorate in Music Performance by the Peck School of Music at the U of Wisconsin, Milwaukee. He also received a Certificate of Significant Achievement in Not Playing the Trombone from the U of Texas at Brownsville with Texas Southmost College.

Recommended for fans of John Fahey, Ry Cooder, Michael Hedges and Peter Lang.

event.title: Mike Cooley (of Drive-By Truckers)

“Cooley sounds as sharp and wise as a Georgia country judge” – Rolling Stone

 

Mike Cooley is an American guitarist, singer, and songwriter. He is best known as a member of the Southern rock band Drive-By Truckers. There, the Alabama musical style blends elements of rock, country, and Americana. Additionally, he is recognized for his sharp, evocative lyrics and distinctive guitar work. As one of the band’s primary songwriters, Cooley has written numerous iconic tracks for Drive-By Truckers. Further, his songs often explore themes of personal introspection, Southern identity, and social commentary. Here, he contributes to their gritty, honest sound and critical success.

The album showcases his storytelling prowess and ability to create poignant, introspective songs with a more stripped-down, intimate sound. Thus, the album represents a rawer sound compared to his work with Drive-By Truckers. Known for his wit and keen observational style, Cooley’s solo work highlights his versatility as an artist. Here, he has cemented his place as an influential figure in contemporary American roots music.

event.title: Asleep At the Wheel
event.description:
“scruffy but sincere traditionalists” – AllMusic

 

Asleep at the Wheel’s Ray Benson has been traversing the globe for over fifty years. He is an ambassador of Western swing music, introducing its irresistible sound to generation after generation. More than 100 musicians have passed through the Wheel, but Benson remains the front man and the keeper of the vision. in the process racking up more than thirty albums, ten Grammy awards and literally millions of miles on the road. 

“I’m the reason it’s still together, but the reason it’s popular is because we’ve had the greatest singers and players,” Benson explains. “When someone joins the band, I say, ‘Learn everything that’s ever been done, then put your own stamp on it.’ I love to hear how they interpret what we do. I’m just a singer and a songwriter, and a pretty good guitar player, but my best talent is convincing people to jump on board and play this music.”

Asleep at the Wheel represents an important cornerstone of American roots music. They maintain this even though some of its members and audiences represent a new generation. That far-reaching appeal remains a testament to Benson’s initial vision.

“It took me sixty years, but I’m doing what I’m meant to do—singing and playing and writing better than I ever have. A bandleader is just someone who gathers people around them to play the best music they can play. I just try and make the best decisions possible and kick some ass every night onstage.”

Recommended for fans of Bob Wills & the Texas Playboys, Kris Kristofferson, Lyle Lovett and Ernest Tubb.

Jason Peterson DeLaire is Linda Peterson’s son. Also, he’s the first of the “next generation” to call music his occupation. Furthermore, he currently tours with Michael Bolton. “What do Prince, Bob Dylan and Stevie Nicks have in common? Those magnificent Petersons.” – Star Tribune

 

Help us celebrate the thirty-seventh anniversary of the Peterson Family Christmas Show! Here, this is a whole family tradition not to be missed. Acclaimed as Minnesota’s First Family of Music, they have also performed locally, nationally, and internationally for many years.

Linda Peterson is an international recording artist, songwriter, pianist and vocalist. Also, Linda has five CDs to her credit. Linda released her latest recording, You Gotta Be Somewhere, in 2015.

Billy Peterson is one of the most celebrated bass players in the world. Moreover, his uncompromising talents as a performer have brought him widespread recognition. Billy has worked Ben Sidran, Carlos Santana, Bob Dylan, Neil Young, Prince, Les Paul, Steve Miller, and many others.

Patty Peterson is a radio personality on KBEM-Jazz88 and executive produces the documentary series “Minnesota Jazz Legends”. Additionally, Patty has received seven coveted Minnesota Music Awards, for best vocalist and best jazz record. Patty has earned an induction into the Minnesota Music Hall of Fame.

Ricky Peterson is one of the most sought-after studio and session keyboard players and producers in America. Furthermore, Ricky tours with Fleetwood Mac, Bonnie Raitt, John Mayer and currently with Stevie Nicks.

Paul Peterson was discovered by Prince at age seventeen. Then, he appeared in the award-winning film Purple Rain, performing with the group The Time. Paul worked with George Benson, Oleta Adams, Anita Baker, and Paula Abdul to name a few. Currently he leads and tours with his St Paul and the Minneapolis Funk All Stars. 

Jason Peterson DeLaire is Linda Peterson’s son. Also, he’s the first of the “next generation” to call music his occupation. Furthermore, he currently tours with Michael Bolton. Also, he worked with Prince, Alexander O’Neal, Richard Marx, Donny Osmond, Oleta Adams, and others. Currently he tours with St Paul and the Minneapolis Funk All Stars.

Recommended for fans of Prince, Steve Miller Band, Stevie Nicks and Donny Osmond.

event.title: Sarah Morris & The Sometimes Elves
event.description:
Just say yes to a sparkly night of holiday favorites with Sarah Morris and the Sometimes Elves!

 

Once a year, Sarah Morris gets out silver bells, the tinsel, the holly, and the jolly. Then, she invites her friends to gather for a sparkling night of holiday music. Also, Morris grew up in a house where Brenda Lee, Johnny Mathis, and Bing Crosby crooned through the family speakers all season long. Thus, Sarah comes by her deep love for Christmas songs honestly. Join Sarah & The Sometimes Elves for a joyful evening filled with festive favorites, love, laughter, and (twinkling) light.

Sarah Morris is a Minneapolis-based Americana singer-songwriter. Here, her crystalline voice and benevolent storytelling have earned her recognition as one of the Midwest’s most compelling musical voices. Many have noticed: Morris won the prestigious Kerrville New Folk Competition in 2018. Additionally, she is three-time Midwest Country Music Organization Songwriter of the Year, and recent MCMO Americana Artist of the Year. Here, Morris creates music that gracefully balances technical precision with profound emotional resonance.

A graduate of the Lawrence University Conservatory of Music, Morris honed her craft in Nashville before returning to Minnesota. Also, her songwriting has garnered national recognition through competitions at Lincoln Center, MerleFest, and the Telluride Troubadour contest. Her albums have earned international airplay and critical acclaim on Americana charts. Moreover, 2023’s Here’s To You earned Album of the Year honors from the Midwest Country Music Organization.

Recommended for fans of Brandi Carlile, Pieta Brown, Patty Griffin and Birds of Chicago.

event.title: Merry Christmas from José James
event.description:
“eclectic, groove-minded jazz singer” – NPR

 

“Merry Christmas from José James” raises the bar for the contemporary Christmas show. James combines the classic jazz-crooner elegance of Frank Sinatra and Nat “King” Cole with the earthy sophistication of soul legends Stevie Wonder and Donny Hathaway. Further, James breathes new life into much-loved holiday classics such as “The Christmas Song”, “White Christmas” and “Let it Snow”. Moreover, the show will feature new compositions by James and his partner Talia Billig. In addition to showcasing his crooner chops, the 50 Shades Darker singer explores his jazz side. The show includes a joyful rendition of John Coltrane’s “My Favorite Things.”

A jazz artist for the hip-hop generation, James artfully blurs the lines between traditional and contemporary jazz, hip-hop, soul, funk, pop and rock. Also, he has released eleven critically acclaimed albums in as many years. Further, James is the recipient of both the Edison Award and L’Académie du Jazz Grand Prix. He has collaborated with many notable artists like Flying Lotus, Robert Glasper, Lalah Hathaway, Ledisi, Aloe Blacc and Jason Moran.

Recommended for fans of Robert Glasper, Meshell Ndegeocello, Lizz Wright and Christian McBride.

📸: Janette Beckman

event.title: A Swingin’ Christmas w/ the Andrew Walesch Big Band
event.description:
“Fresh and classic at the same time” – Star Tribune

 

There’s no better place to be right before Christmas than at Dakota with Andrew Walesch and his eighteen-piece big band. Ring in the holidays with the songs of Bennett, Sinatra, Bublé, Basie, and more!

Like a good many before him, singer and pianist Andrew Walesch manages to encapsulate the sophistication of a cosmopolite and the self-effacing charm of a country boy. Leading his all-star big band, showman Andrew Walesch kidnaps the Blue Eyes tradition and makes it his own in his jazz-bent Sinatra revue. Thus, Walesch is a traditionalist and an iconoclast rolled into one.

Whether composing and arranging or appearing in settings ranging from solo artist to big band, this St. Cloud, MN native is as respectful of his predecessors as he is ready to take a leap into the unknown and chart a new course. Additionally, Andrew routinely jams venues all over the Midwest and beyond with a uniquely cross-generational audience. Walesch’s fans include jazz enthusiasts of a certain age, as well as a younger crowd compelled by his down-home insouciance. Here, all are drawn in by the knowing irreverence of a tried-and-true American nightclub entertainer. 

“Although they are my idols, I don’t attempt to imitate the great pop and jazz artists of the 50s and ’60s,” says Andrew. “But I go for broke when we do our shows – vocally and musically!”

His vocal and piano chops, along with his keen sensibility to find and interpret a great lyric, have led to some great opportunities for Walesch. In 2023, Andrew accepted the position of artistic director of the MIM Music Theater in Phoenix, Arizona where he now resides.  

Recommended for fans of Tony Bennett, Frank Sinatra, Michael Bublé and Bing Crosby.

event.title: The Bad Plus Farewell Tour Finale
event.description:
“finely orchestrated, catchy original tunes, and a knack for radically reconstituted pop covers.” – The New York Times 

 

The Bad Plus are the ultimate originals. A democratic unit with a clear vision and a refusal to conform to convention. For the past two decades, they have played with spirit and adventure and have made their own rules. Moreover, they do so with a bold sense of creativity and intent. Avoiding easy categorization, The Bad Plus has won critical acclaim and a legion of fans worldwide. Further, their unique sound and flair for live performance make them a must-see ensemble.

Now in their twenty-sixth year, The Bad Plus continues to push boundaries. Here, founding members Reid Anderson (bass) and Dave King (drums) embark on a new piano-less incarnation of the band. Also, Ben Monder (guitar) and Chris Speed (tenor saxophone) join the group, instigating a new wave of excitement and anticipation. These new voices are re-energizing their sound and inspiration. The Bad Plus have constantly searched to bridge genres and techniques. Additionally, they explore the infinite possibilities of exceptional musicians working in perfect sync.

The Bad Plus’s sixteenth release, 2024’s Complex Emotions strikes out in stunning new directions. Here, it often sounds radically different than anything the band has done before, while still maintaining the band’s vital and unmistakable identity. Credit that to all four members’ instinctual attraction to song form, the compelling immediacy of their collective improvisations. Also, yes, their willingness to drill down into the full gamut of emotional complexity. The band can veer into so much unexplored terrain yet still emerge sounding like The Bad Plus on Complex Emotions. Thus, this is a testament to their finely crafted identity and insistence on constantly evolving. 

This is The Bad Plus in their most creative and expressive form. This is The Bad Plus now.

Recommended for fans of Brad Mehldau, Joshua Redman, Bill Frisell and Kurt Rosenwinkel.

“finely orchestrated, catchy original tunes, and a knack for radically reconstituted pop covers.” – The New York Times 

 

The Bad Plus are the ultimate originals. A democratic unit with a clear vision and a refusal to conform to convention. For the past two decades, they have played with spirit and adventure and have made their own rules. Moreover, they do so with a bold sense of creativity and intent. Avoiding easy categorization, The Bad Plus has won critical acclaim and a legion of fans worldwide. Further, their unique sound and flair for live performance make them a must-see ensemble.

Now in their twenty-sixth year, The Bad Plus continues to push boundaries. Here, founding members Reid Anderson (bass) and Dave King (drums) embark on a new piano-less incarnation of the band. Also, Ben Monder (guitar) and Chris Speed (tenor saxophone) join the group, instigating a new wave of excitement and anticipation. These new voices are re-energizing their sound and inspiration. The Bad Plus have constantly searched to bridge genres and techniques. Additionally, they explore the infinite possibilities of exceptional musicians working in perfect sync.

The Bad Plus’s sixteenth release, 2024’s Complex Emotions strikes out in stunning new directions. Here, it often sounds radically different than anything the band has done before, while still maintaining the band’s vital and unmistakable identity. Credit that to all four members’ instinctual attraction to song form, the compelling immediacy of their collective improvisations. Also, yes, their willingness to drill down into the full gamut of emotional complexity. The band can veer into so much unexplored terrain yet still emerge sounding like The Bad Plus on Complex Emotions. Thus, this is a testament to their finely crafted identity and insistence on constantly evolving. 

This is The Bad Plus in their most creative and expressive form. This is The Bad Plus now.

Recommended for fans of Brad Mehldau, Joshua Redman, Bill Frisell and Kurt Rosenwinkel.

event.title: Kindred the Family Soul
event.description:
“inspiring melds of soul, R&B, hip-hop, funk, pop… A mindblower.” – AllMusic

 

Kindred the Family Soul is a Grammy-nominated adult contemporary R&B duo from Philadelphia consisting of husband-and-wife Fatin Dantzler and Aja Graydon. Big hit singles elude them, but they maintain a strong following that appreciates their unwavering dedication to releasing relatable, mature R&B. Also, Dantzler and Graydon co-write most of their songs, which are rooted in traditional soul and gospel. 

Dantzler and Graydon began as solo performers. Dantzler was born in Philadelphia and got his start in the music business writing songs for Pebbles and Bell Biv DeVoe. Graydon, from Washington, D.C., signed a solo deal at the age of 15. The two united and began writing songs, but then married and started a family. However, Dantzler went back to trying to make it on the local scene. He and Graydon began performing at the Black Lily club, where they caught the attention of Jill Scott.  

They spent the next two years working on the debut Kindred the Family Soul album, 2003’s Surrender to Love. It featured an impressive cast of collaborators, including Scott, string arranger Larry Gold, Bilal, King Britt, and Jazmine Sullivan. Thus, it was nominated for a Grammy in the category of Best R&B/Soul Album. 2005’s In This Life Together was inspired by Ruby Dee and Ossie Davis’ memoir of the same name. 2008’s The Arrival became their highest-charting title to that point. Here, it reached number sixty-seven on the Billboard 200 and number seven on the R&B Albums chart. 

2011’s Love Has No Recession features guests ranging from go-go pioneer Chuck Brown to relative newcomer BJ the Chicago Kid. Kindred’s sixth full-length, 2016’s Legacy of Love, climbed into the top fifteen of the Billboard R&B chart.

Recommended for fans of Ledisi, Eric Roberson, Avery*Sunshine and Stokley.

event.title: URBAN CLASSIC PRESENTS EARTH, WIND & FIRE
event.description:
Join Minneapolis’ own Urban Classic, led by Michael Bland, for a show dedicated to the music of Earth, Wind & Fire. Prepare to groove as this powerhouse band, featuring a horn section, delivers a high-energy performance of the legendary Earth Wind and Fire funk, soul, and R&B hits. Michael Bland and his band will deliver a powerful and electrifying performance of the EWF major hits. This is a powerhouse performance you won’t want to miss.

Drummer Michael Bland is best known for his work with Prince and the New Power Generation. Starting in 1989, he was a member of NPG. Bland also played with Prince live and on albums for seven years. In 2010, Bland became a member of Nick Jonas & the Administration, a side project of Nick Jonas (Jonas Brothers). Bland worked with Vulfpeck, playing drums on the 2017 single “Hero Town”. Additionally, he has recorded with Cory Wong several times. Bland is also a member of Soul Asylum.

Geoff LeCrone, guitar (Dr. Mambo’s Combo/Andrew Walesch Orchestra)
Scott Agster, trombone
Riley Helgeson, trumpet
Josh May, trumpet
John Bertsch, saxophone

event.title: Rebirth Brass Band
event.description:
“there is not a band on earth that is better. Stunning.” – Flea, Red Hot Chili Peppers

 

For almost four decades, the Grammy-winning Rebirth Brass Band has been “stunning” fans. Further, they are loved worldwide for their fiery live shows and rich musical catalog. Their trademark sound pays homage to the New Orleans brass band tradition. Also, they weave a tapestry that combines elements of jazz, funk, soul, R&B. Then, they incorporate more of the sounds from the streets they grew up on. Their sound has traveled from their legendary twenty-five-year run of Tuesday nights at the Maple Leaf to stages all over the world. Rebirth is the soundtrack of the Crescent City and her premier musical ambassador.

Rebirth was founded by brothers Phil and Keith Frazier over thirty-five years ago. They began their career playing on the sidewalks of the French Quarter and quickly landed gigs at second line parades. Those auspicious beginnings have led to thousands of shows to music aficionados everywhere, including heads of state and royalty.

The band’s unique “soundtrack of New Orleans” has also garnered admiration from artists of all genres. They’ve shared the stage and collaborated with everyone from the Grateful Dead to the Red Hot Chili Peppers. Also, Maceo Parker, Green Day, U2, James Brown, 311, G-Love, MuteMath, Juvenile, Train, Big Freedia, Ani DiFranco, and Galactic. Further, Allen Toussaint, Neville Brothers, Quincy Jones and Trombone Shorty.

Recommended for fans of Trombone Shorty, The Dirty Dozen Brass Band, Kermit Ruffins and Preservation Hall Jazz Band.

event.title: Steely Dane
event.description:
“the band is energetic and sounds amazing” – Milwaukee Magazine

 

In 2010, co-founders David Adler and David Stoler (The Steely Daves) put together a tribute show for Steely Dan. There, they would feature the best musicians in the Madison, WI music scene. Madison is located in Dane County, WI, thus the name. 

The first Steely Dane show featured over thirty of Madison’s best rock and jazz musicians, and it sold out. Not ones to waste a herculean effort of arranging a full night’s worth of the Dan’s best stuff, the crew decided to do it again, and again… and oops, now it’s no longer a show, it’s a BAND. 

Since then, the band has trimmed down to the current fourteen-piece family. Now, that features a four-piece horn section, two female backup singers, two guitars, two keyboards, vibes, and percussion. Here, they have all the instruments necessary to recreate the amazing mixes of the Dan’s albums and live performances. Moreover, the band has won multiple awards for best tribute band and sold out theaters from Chicago to Minneapolis. Additionally, they are a perennial favorite at summer festivals as well. 

Their songbook features over fifty songs from both Steely Dan and Donald Fagen’s solo career. This allows them to play different shows night after night. Furthermore, they have even performed complete album shows for The Royal Scam, Aja, and Gaucho.

Recommended for fans of Steely Dan, Donald Fagen, Fleetwood Mac and The Eagles.

event.title: Marcus Miller
event.description:
“one of the cornerstones of modern electric bass” – Premier Guitar

 

Get ready for an unforgettable evening with Grammy-winning bass virtuoso, Marcus Miller! Celebrating over forty-three years of musical excellence, Marcus will be performing selections from his extensive catalog. Here, he features beloved hits that have graced the careers of Miles Davis, David Sanborn, Roberta Flack, and Luther Vandross. Moreover, prepare to be captivated as Marcus infuses each piece of music with his unparalleled arranging skills. He delivers fresh and exciting interpretations of his music that keep audiences on their toes.

Marcus’ resume speaks for itself. There, he has dozens of movie scores and over 500 recording credits to his name across jazz, R&B, and opera. Also, as a UNESCO Artist for Peace and changemaker, his work on social justice projects continues to be inspiring. In 2020, Marcus created, musically produced, and posted the “Lift Every Voice” get out the vote event. There, he brought together political leaders and musical legends to encourage political participation. Additionally, he contributed to UNESCO’s United Against Racism video alongside countless industry legends. Then, Prince Albert of Monaco commissioned him to create the orchestral arrangement for in Donny Hathaway’s “Someday We’ll All Be Free” video, which he also appeared in.

The year ahead continues to look just as busy for Marcus. Further, he is a member of the Board of Directors for the Herbie Hancock Institute of Jazz. Also, he joined Herbie for a virtual celebration of International Jazz Day on April 30th. In 2022, Marcus composed the score for the documentary film SIDNEY for Apple TV+. There, the film told the story of legendary actor, filmmaker and iconic civil rights activist, Sidney Poitier.

Recommended for fans of Miles Davis, Victor Wooten, Stanley Clarke and Jaco Pastorius.

event.title: Trio Mandili
event.description:
The world’s most viral folk trio.

 

How does a centuries-old village singing tradition become a 1-billion-view global digital phenomenon?

Meet Trio Mandili — arguably the world’s most viral folk trio.

What began as three friends singing together in the Georgian countryside grew into an extraordinary international success story. Their three-part harmonies are rooted in Georgia’s ancient polyphonic singing tradition. Accompanied by the traditional panduri, they have captivated audiences across cultures and languages.

The trio has grown quickly, garnering more than one billion views worldwide and nearly two million YouTube subscribers. Trio Mandili has built a global following extending far beyond Georgia and the Caucasus and now performs around the world.

In 2027, the trio brings its unforgettable live performance to the United States for the first time.

Whether you’ve followed their videos for years or are discovering them for the first time, this is a rare opportunity to experience the voices behind more than a billion views — live.

Recommended for fans of DakhaBrakha, Basiani Ensemble, Bani and Chveneburebi.

The Triple Crown Volleyball NIT returns to Kansas City February 12–15, 2027, bringing one of the nation’s premier youth volleyball tournaments to the Kansas City Convention Center and surrounding venues. This elite girls volleyball event features top club teams from across the country, with more than 680 teams, 8,000 athletes and 1,000+ college coaches expected to be in attendance.

Athletes will compete across multiple age divisions in a high-level tournament environment designed for competition, exposure and development. The event includes college camps on Friday, followed by tournament play February 13–15, giving teams, coaches, families and fans an exciting weekend of volleyball action in downtown Kansas City.

Whether you are cheering on an athlete, scouting future talent or experiencing one of the country’s top club volleyball events, the Triple Crown Volleyball NIT offers a dynamic championship atmosphere and a major showcase for the next generation of volleyball standouts.

event.title: Sparkle #8 / A Performance by Ayana Evans
event.venue_json: {"id":5134,"global_id":"camstl.org?id=5134","venue":"Contemporary Art Museum St. Louis","address":"3750 Washington Blvd","city":"St. Louis","country":"United States","state":"MO","zip":"63108","website":"https://camstl.org","phone":"314-535-0770","url":"https://camstl.org/venue/contemporary-art-museum-st-louis/","geo_lat":38.6405635,"geo_lng":-90.2349529,"show_map":true,"show_map_link":true}
event.description:
In conjunction with her exhibition Nobody’s Gonna Love You the Way I Do, Ayana Evans presents a newly commissioned live performance that brings her distinctive unapologetic, emotionally invigorating, and deeply improvisatory practice to attendees. 

Sparkle #8 unfolds in CAM’s Performance Space among Evans’s exhibition, welcoming audiences to interact directly with Evans. During these performances, Evans typically assigns both individual and collective tasks that turn audience members from viewers to participants, and which speak to relevant and pressing concerns. Evans’s performances are vehicles through which she challenges the ways class, race, gender, and sex are implicated in prevailing sociopolitical attitudes.

event.title: C.R.E.A.M. Fair
event.venue_json: {"id":5134,"global_id":"camstl.org?id=5134","venue":"Contemporary Art Museum St. Louis","address":"3750 Washington Blvd","city":"St. Louis","country":"United States","state":"MO","zip":"63108","website":"https://camstl.org","phone":"314-535-0770","url":"https://camstl.org/venue/contemporary-art-museum-st-louis/","geo_lat":38.6405635,"geo_lng":-90.2349529,"show_map":true,"show_map_link":true}
event.description:
In conjunction with her exhibition Nobody’s Gonna Love You the Way I Do, Ayana Evans brings her ongoing community engagement project C.R.E.A.M. (Cash Rules Everything Around Me) to St. Louis. Part block party and part opportunity fair, C.R.E.A.M. connects community members—such as students, job seekers, queer activists, artists, and people affected by the justice system—with free resources and supportive services. Whether you, someone you love, or members of your community are looking for helpful paths forward, come to the C.R.E.A.M. Fair for a joyful communal space centered on care, creativity, and collective support. Bright, comfortable clothes are encouraged—no suits allowed!

Schedule

10:00 am / The C.R.E.A.M. Fair opens with the following offerings:

• Engage in an interactive art activity with Freedom Arts & Education Center
• Discover the cultural resources of 4theVille, Show Me The World, and The Black Rep
• Learn how Keyway Center for Diversion & Reentry offers assistance on housing stability, financial security, emotional wellness, and community reengagement
• Explore Mission: St. Louis’s Beyond Jobs program for individuals seeking meaningful employment, career advancement, and opportunities to build greater stability
• Sign up with St. Louis Public Library to get a library card and access to Tech Connect services, including website development, resume writing, and Creative Experience (recording rooms, 3D printers, laser cutters, digital creative software, and more!)
• Meet with admissions representatives from Harris-Stowe State University, Ranken Technical College, and Webster University
• Access health resources from the St. Louis City Health Department

10:00–11:30 am / Play Date drop-in art activity

11:00 am / Performance by Harris Stowe State University Honeycombs and The Swarm Drumline

11:30 am–2:00 pm / Complimentary food

12:00–12:30 pm / Resume-writing and job-search workshop with St. Louis Public Library

12:00–1:00 pm / Free headshots with Tyler Small

12:30 pm / Art + Wellness with Nico Marie

1:00 pm / Panel Discussion with Chloe Bass and Hayveyah McGowan, moderated by Ayana Evans

2:00 pm / Step performance by Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity Inc.

2:30 pm / Closing Remarks

This event is free and open to the public. Registration is encouraged; please click here to sign up.

  • Seating is available for the 10:00 am and 12:00 pm workshops and 1:00 pm panel discussion on a first come, first served basis. If you require seating, please email programs@camstl.org to reserve a seat.
  • Light lunch is available for free, drinks and additional food are available for purchase at the café.

event.title: CAM Trivia Night
event.venue_json: {"id":5134,"global_id":"camstl.org?id=5134","venue":"Contemporary Art Museum St. Louis","address":"3750 Washington Blvd","city":"St. Louis","country":"United States","state":"MO","zip":"63108","website":"https://camstl.org","phone":"314-535-0770","url":"https://camstl.org/venue/contemporary-art-museum-st-louis/","geo_lat":38.6405635,"geo_lng":-90.2349529,"show_map":true,"show_map_link":true}
event.description:
Fall in Love with CAM
Saturday, November 14, 2026
7:00–10:00 pm
Doors open at 6:00 pm

Assemble a team of the best and brightest to have fun showing off your trivia knowledge!

Hosted by the multi-talented Marina May Schleicher, a self-described STL hypegirl and co-host of the cool WIP podcast, our annual Trivia Night raises funds to support CAM’s free youth art education programs. Bring your own food and enjoy drinks from an open bar. In addition to a trivia contest, guests may compete in other party games like the infamous Booze Tower Ring Toss and Heads or Tails to win fabulous prizes. Bid on speciality items from local artists, makers, and restaurants in the silent auction. Special thanks to Schlafly Beer.

The evening will include:

  • 8 Rounds of trivia featuring questions about pop culture, art, and more
  • Bring your own food and enjoy an open bar
  • Party games like Heads or Tails and the popular Booze Tower Ring Toss, where attendees can win their favorite libation
  • A silent auction with items from local artists, makers, and restaurants
  • Mulligans available for purchase

Tickets and Sponsorships

Tickets are $500 for a table of 10 people and include an open bar. This is a 21+ event.

Buy Now

Sponsorships start at $1,250 with other additional options for in-kind support. Sponsors at the VIP level and above are provided with deluxe snacks. Presenting sponsors will receive table service. For information about sponsorship opportunities, email Director of Development Sherry Thomas or call 314.535.0770 x213.

About the Emcee

Marina May Schleicher is a writer, curator, communications strategist, semi-professional talker, and self-described STL hype-girl. She co-founded Silver Space [rebranded to cool WIP], an independent editorial platform focused on contemporary art and culture, and co-hosts the cool WIP podcast, which features conversations with artists, curators, and cultural organizers. May Schleicher is the current Gallery Director of Opaque Collective where she organizes exhibitions, helps to develop public programming, and co-leads marketing and communications alongside the members. Across all the projects, her work consistently emphasizes collaboration and connection across artists, institutions, collectors, and audiences. Her writing and projects can be found at coolwipofficial.com.

event.title: ZM (Zombie Musical)
event.description:
New Line Theatre opens its 35th season with the American premiere of this gloriously unhinged new meta-musical from certified chaos merchants Mark Hollmann and Greg Kotis — the Tony-winning mad geniuses who looked at musical theatre and said, “What if… but weirder?”

Part Walking Dead, part Bat Boy, and part “you probably shouldn’t eat that,” ZM is a darkly comic fable set in an American small town where a fast-food chain is test-marketing a new sandwich. Which turns customers into zombies. Two brave teenage employees must risk everything to infiltrate corporate headquarters, uncover the truth, and maybe — just maybe — ask, “Should we have read the ingredients list?”

Originally formed in 2021, The Fresh Bears are a band of three brothers with talent and experience beyond their years, and a love for music. Hailing from Valparaiso IN, The Fresh Bears released their debut album in 2025. “POVERTY SOUL” not only showcases their musical prowess and songwriting ability, but the mark that they are destined to make on the music industry and anyone they come in contact with.

Saint Chuck is a St. Louis based “indie pop” band comprised of Austin Shariff, Hannah Wozniak and James Mettrick. In 2025, the band expanded its core lineup to include guitarist Tyler Mauer and bassist Anthony Mauer.

event.title: Book Talk with Sonny Buttar, author of Daughters of Rosebud
event.description:
Left Bank Books and the Left Bank Books Foundation are delighted to present St. Louisan Sonny Buttar’s debut novel, The Daughters of Rosebud (2026).
Join us at High Low Literary Arts Cafe to welcome Sonny Buttar for a presentation and book signing, free and open to the public. Sonny will be in conversation with St. Louis author and Board Chair of Kimbilio for Black Fiction, David Haynes.

The Daughters of Rosebud is a powerful exploration of sisterhood, family loyalty, and the courage it takes to heal. Teacher Salma Chaudhry lives a quiet life, avoiding all attachments. Growing up in small-town Rosebud, Salma and her older sister Asma were inseparable, but amid their mother’s decline and their parents’ rigid expectations, Asma makes a choice that tears the family apart. The fallout changes everything–and forces Salma to choose between her sister and her parents. Salma has spent years trying to forget. But as she recollects her past and considers reconciliation with her father, a young student opens a surprising connection to Asma’s past. In finally facing her history, Salma finds the bravery to love and hope again.

event.title: SOLD OUT Intro to Leksand-style Embroidery Workshop with Kirsi Manni
event.description:
This program is sold out. To be added to the waitlist, please call 612-871-4907. 

Try out Leksand style embroidery with visiting artist Kirsi Manni, a textile expert and teacher visiting from Dalarna, Sweden! In this one-day introductory-level class, students will practice some basics embroidery and applique techniques to create a small sampler that can be put to use as a pin cushion, needle case front, or other project. Students will also make their own colorful pom-pom or tuppa, typical of Leksand-style folk dress. While they work, students will have a chance to hear from Kirsi about her experience working with textiles in Sweden, as well as view examples of historic needlework from ASI’s material collection and Kirsi’s personal collection.

Kirsi Manni is the owner of Art&Craft Sweden and lives in Siljanäs, Dalarna. Over one week this fall, Kirsi will bring her expertise in Leksand style folk dress to ASI. Kirsi is also offering a more intensive needlework project workshop and a talk about her personal experience with folk costume traditions.

Additional information:
  • Advanced registration required.
  • A $15 materials fee is included in the class fee and includes all necessary materials.
  • Students are encouraged to bring a small sewing kit with their favorite hand sewing tools, including a pair of fabric shears and small thread scissors, assorted needles and pins, and a thimble if they use one. Students should also bring magnification (i.e.; readers) if they use them for close work.
Prerequisites:
  • Ages: Suitable for ages 18+.
  • Skill level: This workshop welcomes students of all experience levels, but students will progress further with this project if they have previous hand sewing experience.
  • Physical Ability: This class requires good hand and finger dexterity and the ability to sit for long periods of time.

event.title: Lille Fredag x SACC: An Evening of Kubb
event.description:
Join the Swedish American Chamber of Commerce (SACC) and Lille Fredag, a monthly mixer bringing together young adults with Nordic heritage, for an evening of Kubb in the American Swedish Institute courtyard.

Eric Anderson and his team from the U.S. National Kubb Championship will kick off the evening with a brief introduction to the history of Kubb and a demonstration of how to play, with lessons and open play continuing throughout the evening.

event.title: October Open Nordic Jam
event.description:
Join us on the first Thursday of every month for Open Nordic Jam!

Have you ever wanted to play music in the historic Turnblad Mansion? Now’s your chance! Bring your nyckelharpa, hardingfele, fiddle, or any acoustic instrument to ASI’s Open Nordic Jam. This jam is open to musicians of all levels who want to learn and play Nordic folk music. Bring your friends or plan to make new ones here!

Minnesota has long been known for its rich music scenes—in part due to the many immigrant diasporas that have established themselves in the area. From Nisswa-stämman to the Nordic Roots festival, to the countless house jams across the state, Nordic folk music is an important part of Minnesota’s musical identity. Whether you’re a master fiddler or want to learn more about folk music, this monthly gathering is for you!

This jam is facilitated by ASI staff, but tunes are selected each time by musicians in the room. We will play standards and originals inspired by the folk traditions of Sweden, Norway, Finland, Denmark, and Iceland. While many musicians may bring traditional instruments, all acoustic instrumentalists are welcome to participate. If you do not play an instrument, you can still attend if you respectfully observe and listen. Dancing is encouraged but not required—see you there! No advanced registration required.

event.description:

Enjoy four historic Thursday evenings with Jessica Karlsson, an ASI Language Instructor and Historian, this October. In this lecture series, participants will meet four intriguing Swedish Icons and learn about their lasting impact on the world through an historic lens. Suffragettes, diplomats, champions of childrens’ rights, inventors, and more, don’t miss this opportunity to dive into history and get to know these Swedish greats!

Oct 1 – Astrid Lindgren, 1907–2002
Mostly known as the author of Pippi Longstocking, Astrid Lindgren was a prolific and far-reaching author of childrens’ books translated across the globe, as well as a champion of childrens’ rights.

Oct 8 – Raoul Wallenberg, 1912–unknown
Raoul Wallenberg became a Swedish Diplomat who traveled to Budapest and saved tens of thousands of Jews during the Holocaust in 1944 before ultimately disappearing.

Oct 22 – Selma Lagerlöf, 1858–1940
Lagerlöf was not only the first woman ever to receive the Nobel Prize in literature in 1909, but also was an active member in the Swedish suffrage movement and stood up for the underserved in society.

Oct 29 – Alfred Nobel 1833–1896
Alfred Nobel is best known as the inventor of dynamite and the founder of the prestigious Nobel Prize but was also an intriguing figure of contrasts.

Additional information:

  • No materials or knowledge of Swedish required.
  • Instructor will use slideshows in combination with printed materials.
  • Advance registration required.

event.title: Nordic Music Workshop: Polska of the People with Renee Vaughan
event.description:
Join Renee Vaughan for free workshop for musicians, Polska of the People: Hello Groove!

Come explore the unique rhythms of Swedish folk music, the polska in all her glorious forms. This is an open and supportive space for musicians of all instruments and experience levels who want to better understand what makes a tune belong to the greater Swedish polska family. We’ll explore the basic rhythmic framework of polska, how the music relates to the dance, and the different ways musicians can find their own way within it. We’ll learn a couple of very accessible groovy tunes from Södermanland to get us started. Bring your instruments. All instruments welcome, all experience levels welcome. You are also welcome to come listen and learn.

Renee’s been playing Swedish folk music for nearly 20 years and have always been drawn to its rhythms and melodies. This summer, she studied Swedish folk music with master musicians Cajsa Ekstav and Christina Frohm, as well as traditional Swedish dance with master dance instructor Bert Persson and is bringing that learning back to the Twin Cities. This program is supported by the American Scandinavian Foundation.

event.title: Exploring Traditional Wooden Boatbuilding Techniques with Brian Thorkildson
event.description:
Wooden boats are fascinating objects—get just a taste of some of the traditional techniques needed to build them in this evening-long workshop. Students will have the opportunity to get hands on with specialty tools to make a small sample cross-section of a traditional Nordic wooden boat. With hand planes, students will cut bevels on their planks and shape a frame section. Students will also make their own tree nails—the wooden nails that held the planks to the frames—and assemble their samples with rivets and trees nails into a small cross section of traditional Nordic boat. No past woodworking experience needed; this class is perfect for anyone excited about wood, boats, history, or tools to try out something new.

event.description:
Knit a headband with a traditional Bjärbo pattern in this afternoon-long workshop! Learn about the Binge (pronounced “Bing-ah”) tradition of knitting from Southwest Sweden’s Halland province. This style dates to the 1600s and is characterized by colorwork patterns and colors similar to Fair Isle, and is often knit in a double-thickness fabric. In the workshop, students will knit a wide ski headband using a traditional Bjärbo design motif from the Halland province. After a short presentation, fiber artist Wendy Johnson will lead students through the steps of knitting the headband on circular needles. Students will need to complete their headband at home. The finished headband is perfect for keeping heads warm as the days get cold or to give as a gift!

Additional information:

  • Advanced registration required.

  • If knitting this as a gift, make sure to measure the gift recipient’s head in advance!
  • Students should bring a set of U.S. size 3 24-inch circular knitting needles. Optionally, you may want to bring stitch markers, scissors, or other knitting notions you prefer to use.

 

Prerequisites:

  • Skill level: Intermediate knitters. Students must have basic knitting skills, with experience casting on, the knit and purl stitches, and binding off, to be successful with this project.

event.title: Picture Weaving on a Rigid Heddle Loom Workshop with Kerstin Neumüller
event.description:
This course is online and will take place over two days, Sat, October 17 and Sun, October 18 from 10 am-12 pm Central Time both sessions.

Join Swedish textile artist and educator Kerstin Neumüller for two online sessions focused on weaving a weft-facing repp band on a small rigid heddle-style band weaving loom. This type of weave uses the same tools as a warp-facing repp, but a different technique. Instead of pulling the warp tight with the weft, students will learn to give the weft more space and create a pattern that is built up as you weave, much like drawing or picture. Kerstin will share various possible patterns, giving students a starting place for designing their own band. This virtual class is an excellent option for students who have practiced band weaving on their own or in other classes with Kerstin. Students will work alongside Kerstin as she covers project options for small looms, materials, and tips for weft-faced weaving from her book Simple Weave. This versatile technique can also be used to create picture weavings on a frame loom for larger projects!

Additional information:

Norwegian-style acanthus carvings are familiar to many appreciators of traditional Norwegian buildings, wooden ware, and other folk art—but before you can carve it, you have to be able to draw it! Join woodcarver Jock Holmen for a five-week class to learn the basic “alphabet” of Norwegian carving, first through drawing and then with chisels and gouges. event.title: Exhibit G Book Talk with Fady Joudah
event.description:
Join a reading and conversation with award-winning poet and translator Fady Joudah, presented by Milkweed Editions.

About EXHIBIT G: Fady Joudah writes from the split perspective of a Palestinian American physician caring for the sick while watching the destruction of Gaza from the United States, a nation complicit in that destruction. He locates the paradox of his position everywhere: in the seed a sparrow eats from his proffered hand; in his writing in English, the oppressor’s language; in the faces of Palestinian children receiving meals from aid kitchens—a glimpse into what his life could have been, and what is being lost in a war disproportionately impacting children and their families. Throughout the book, beauty insists on its survival not only through the Palestinian people, but also through the nonhuman world in which he takes occasional refuge from the devastation that humanity brings upon itself.

About the author: Fady Joudah is the author of […], a finalist for the National Book Award and winner of the Lenore Marshall Poetry Prize, and Exhibit G. His other poetic works include: The Earth in the Attic; Alight; Textu, a book-long sequence of short poems whose meter is based on cellphone character count; Footnotes in the Order of Disappearance; and Tethered to Stars. He has translated several collections of poetry from the Arabic and is the co-editor and co-founder of the Etel Adnan Poetry Prize. He was a winner of the Yale Series of Younger Poets competition and has received the Jackson Poetry Prize, a PEN award, a Banipal/Times Literary Supplement prize from the UK, the Griffin Poetry Prize, a Guggenheim Fellowship, and the Arab American Book Award. He lives in Houston, with his wife and kids, where he practices internal medicine.

We’ll also touch upon how environment, migration, and trade have changed and preserved food traditions in both Scandinavia and Scandinavian American communities over the past 150 years. event.title: Babies at the Castle: Eyes as Big as Plates
event.description:
Caregivers and infants up to 18 months are invited to experience the surreal photography of Finnish-Norwegian artists Riitta Ilkonen and Karoline Hjorth in the exhibition Eyes as Big as Plates. The exhibition presents whimsical portraits of people in harmony with nature and invites moments of wonder, curiosity, and connection while exploring ideas of identity, belonging, and place.

In the exhibition, ASI educators will guide caregivers and babies through each stop offering simple, age-appropriate activities that encourage looking closely, noticing details, and responding together. Caregivers carry infants at eye level and leave strollers behind, creating an up-close experience with each artwork that supports shared attention and early visual exploration.

Each thirty-minute tour offers a unique experience. Because not every stop can be included, the October tour may feature different works of art and different activities than the July tour, giving returning visitors something new to discover. The program continues with 15 minutes of sensory play in the Castle before it opens to the public, extending the experience beyond the gallery through hands-on exploration designed for caregivers and babies.

Additional information:

  • Admission is included, allowing participants to explore the exhibition, the Turnblad Mansion, the Family Gallery, and ASI’s outdoor, fenced-in spaces after the program.
  • Advanced registration is required.
  • ASI educators determine whether to run or cancel programs based on registration levels on the Friday before the scheduled prgoram date. Please register by Friday, October 16, if interested in attending.
  • The experience encourages caregivers and babies to slow down together, observe closely, and respond to what they see. Through this shared looking, the tour fosters curiosity, imagination, and early developmental growth in a setting designed for connection.
  • Advanced registration required.

event.title: Lovikka-Inspired Knit Mittens Workshop with Wendy Johnson
event.description:
Take a deep dive into the Lovikka knitting tradition, known for its unique embroidered cuff embellishments! In this half day workshop, students will explore the rich history of this renowned tradition originally from the town of Lovikka, located near the Arctic Circle. After a short presentation, fiber artist Wendy Johnson will lead students in the steps of how to knit the mitten on double-pointed needles, embroider the cuffs, and “full” (lightly felt) a miniature version of the Lovikka mitten. The mitten completed in class is a child’s size, though the provided pattern includes an adult-sized mitten that you may complete at home. These embellished mittens are sure to keep you cozy in the cold season or provide the perfect seasonal gift!

Additional information:

  • Advanced registration required.
  • A $35 materials fee covers the pattern, one skein of Lovikka yarn (enough for two mini-sized mittens), and embroidery yarn.
  • Students should bring a set of U.S. size 9 double-pointed needles (preferably in a set of 5), stitch markers with loop closure (or medium-sized safety pins), a small stitch holder, and a tapestry needle.

 

Prerequisites

  • Skill level: Intermediate knitters. This is an appropriate project for knitters new to mittens, but students should know how to knit in the round on double-pointed needles and provide their own needles and notions.
  • Ages: Suitable for ages 16+. A discounted ticket price for ages 16-17 is available at checkout.

event.title: Nordic Book Circle
event.description:
Contemporary Nordic literature is full of diverse literary voices, styles, and genres. This September 2026 through May 2027 the ASI Nordic Book Circle will gather monthly, in-person, to read and discuss a work of Nordic literature in English translation. Our focus this year will be on works of literature written by women authors from across the Nordic world. The works we read will chronologically trace books penned between 1912 and 2020, and include two winners of the Nobel Prize in Literature; authors from the countries of Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Iceland, Greenland; various genres; and a range of topics and perspectives.

If you love to read and discuss literature and would like to expand your appreciation of literature from various parts of the world (the Nordic world in particular), we would love to have you join! Limited to 20 attendees; please register in advance.

Following up on our previous AI event in February 2026, the Swedish American Chamber of Commerce Minnesota (SACC-MN) is revisiting AI at a time when the technology and its role in business are evolving faster than ever.

Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping how organizations operate, but separating the hype from real, positive, and scalable impact has never been more important.

Join SACC-MN for an evening of expert insights and real-world perspectives exploring AI Transformation in Global and Local Business.

Through five short keynote presentations followed by a moderated panel discussion and Q &A. attendees will explore the current state of AI in business leadership and workforce transformation from startups to Fortune 500 enterprises.

  • Quinton Krueger – Intellectual Property in AI

  • Jenny Larsson – AI Implementation in Global Business
  • Dr. Toby J. Velte – Leadership & Workforce Transformation in the Age of AI

event.title: Scandinavian Everyday Book Talk with Nichole Accettola
event.description:
Welcome back Nichole Accettola to hear about her newest cookbook, Scandinavian Everyday: Vibrant, Simple Meals from Northern Europe, in conversation with Minnesota-based chef and author Amy Thielen. A chef and IACP award-winning author, Nichole has much to share about how contemporary Scandinavian cuisine offers a simple, sustainable, and satisfying approach to cooking and eating at home. In this book talk, Nichole and Amy will discuss Nichole’s years of living in Denmark, running Kantine restaurant in San Francisco, and her journey to becoming a cookbook author, as well as a few hints for favorite recipes from the book.

 

Additional information:

  • A Q&A and opportunity for book signing will follow the discussion.
  • Guests may also be interested in an opportunity to cook alongside Nichole in an intimate afternoon workshop
  • Advanced registration encouraged, tickets at the door if available.

 

About the presenters:

Nichole Accettola is a CIA-trained chef with years of experience in both professional kitchens and teaching culinary arts, abroad in Denmark as well as in the US. As the owner of Kantine, a Scandinavian-inspired café located in San Francisco, Nichole showcases her gorgeous pastries, porridges and jewel-like smørrebrød sandwiches which have garnered glowing reviews from media such as San Francisco Chronicle, Time Out, and Eater.

Nichole Accettola is also the author of Scandinavian from Scratch: A Love Letter to the Baking of Denmark, Norway and Sweden, an IACP award winning cookbook. Scandinavian from Scratch and Scandinavian Everyday are both available from the ASI Museum Store.

Follow Nichole on Instagram @nicholeate and keep up with her new book @scandinavianfromscratch

Amy Thielen is a two-time James Beard Award-winning writer, cookbook author, and chef. Her books include The New Midwestern Table, the memoir Give a Girl a Knife, and Company: The Radically Casual Art of Cooking for Others. Her cooking show, Heartland Table, ran on Food Network from 2013 to 2015, and she is currently the host of Ham Radio, a podcast and live on-air cooking show in partnership with KAXE/KBXE, Northern Community Radio, Grand Rapids/Bemidji. Amy lives in Park Rapids, Minnesota with her husband, Aaron Spangler, and their son, where she is a board member of the Nemeth Art Center.

Follow Amy on Instagram and Twitter at @amyrosethielen

event.title: November Open Nordic Jam
event.description:
Join us on the first Thursday of every month for Open Nordic Jam!

Have you ever wanted to play music in the historic Turnblad Mansion? Now’s your chance! Bring your nyckelharpa, hardingfele, fiddle, or any acoustic instrument to ASI’s Open Nordic Jam. This jam is open to musicians of all levels who want to learn and play Nordic folk music. Bring your friends or plan to make new ones here!

Minnesota has long been known for its rich music scenes—in part due to the many immigrant diasporas that have established themselves in the area. From Nisswa-stämman to the Nordic Roots festival, to the countless house jams across the state, Nordic folk music is an important part of Minnesota’s musical identity. Whether you’re a master fiddler or want to learn more about folk music, this monthly gathering is for you!

This jam is facilitated by ASI staff, but tunes are selected each time by musicians in the room. We will play standards and originals inspired by the folk traditions of Sweden, Norway, Finland, Denmark, and Iceland. While many musicians may bring traditional instruments, all acoustic instrumentalists are welcome to participate. If you do not play an instrument, you can still attend if you respectfully observe and listen. Dancing is encouraged but not required—see you there! No advanced registration required.

event.title: Weaving the Skruck Basket Workshop with Ty Sheaffer
event.description:
This class runs Fri, Nov 6, from 6-8 pm, and Sat and Sun, Nov 7-8, 9 am-5 pm each day

Weave a unique splint basket from Sweden’s Hälsingland province, the skruck basket, in this weekend-long workshop. Originally a practical pack style basket, a skruck is a splint basket made from split willow and ash, and unusual in that it is woven from the rim down. On Friday night, class will gather for an orientation to the basket, tools, and classroom. On Saturday, students will try out processing willow splints themselves using a brake from Sweden, prepare their weaving material from ash and willow, and prepare their basket rim. On Sunday, students will weave and finish their baskets. Throughout the weekend, additional topics will be discussed such as materials harvesting, specialty tools, and some Scandinavian basketry history.

Additional information:

  • This class runs Friday, November 6 from 6-8 pm, and Saturday and Sunday, November 7-8, 9 am-5 pm both days.
  • Advanced registration required. A discounted ticket price for ages 14-17 is available at checkout.
  • A materials fee of $50 is due in class to instructor Ty Sheaffer and covers all the tools and materials for one small basket. The size of the completed basket will vary based on each’s student’s pace; most students will complete a basket about 8” tall.
  • Students may also bring their own work gloves and a Mora style carving knife, if they have one.

 

Prerequisites:

  • Physical ability: Basketry requires average hand strength and dexterity to complete a project, such as being able to open a jam jar.
  • Skill level: This course welcomes students of all skill levels.
  • Ages: Suitable for ages 16+, or 14-15 registered alongside an accompanying adult. A discounted ticket price for youth 14-17 is available at checkout.
