event.title: Babies at the Castle
event.description:
Share Swedish art and culture with your baby during a morning of exploration at the Turnblad Mansion.

Caregivers and infants up to 18 months are invited to experience ASI’s annual holiday experience, Remember When, in the historic Turnblad Mansion. During this special tour, babies and their caregivers explore festive displays, discover stories from the past, and engage with the sights, sounds, and details of the holiday season together. Through close looking, shared attention, and simple activities, families build meaningful connections with art, history, and each other.

ASI educator Jason Leuthold guides caregivers and babies through each stop, offering age-appropriate activities that encourage curiosity, exploration, and engagement. Caregivers carry infants at eye level, allowing babies to experience artwork and installations up close while supporting early visual exploration and shared discovery. Each 30-minute tour offers a unique experience and concludes with 15 minutes of sensory play in the Castle before it opens to the public at 10 am.

event.title: Momma’s Chirstmas Gift: A Kao Kalia Yang Book Talk
event.description:
Join local author Kao Kalia Yang for a special reading of her new book: Momma’s Christmas Gift.

Kao Kalia Yang returns to ASI this November with Momma’s Christmas Gift, a heartfelt story that celebrates family, generosity, and love during the Christmas season. Families are invited to join this local author for an intergenerational reading experience featuring projected images from the book.

Momma’s Christmas Gift is a modern retelling of The Gift of the Magi that follows a Hmong refugee family celebrating Christmas while navigating financial hardships and the sacrifices made out of love. Through gentle, lyrical storytelling, Kao Kalia Yang explores the universal experiences of family, resilience, generosity, and the deep care parents hold for their children. This 30-minute reading invites children and their grown-ups to reflect on themes of kindness, belonging, and the many ways families show love.

Following the reading, Kao Kalia Yang will participate in a Q&A and sign books. The book is best suited for children ages 4-8.

Copies of Momma’s Christmas Gift will be available for purchase in the Museum Store. Families are encouraged to purchase a copy before the program begins, as supplies may be limited.

About the author:
Kao Kalia Yang is a Hmong American author whose work includes award-winning memoirs and children’s books, including The Latehomecomer: A Hmong Family Memoir, A Map Into the World, The Shared Room, and The Most Beautiful Thing. Her writing has received recognition from organizations including the National Endowment for the Arts, the National Book Critics Circle, the American Library Association, and the Minnesota Book Awards.

Additional information:

  • Upon arrival, check in at the front desk, where Visitor Service Associates will provide directions to Larson Hall.
  • Museum admission is included with registration.

event.description:
Join us for a special, puppet-filled edition of Kids at the Castle featuring Seth Eberle.

Seth Eberle returns to ASI with Dream of Owls, an imaginative puppet performance that helps families explore fear, curiosity, and the power of learning. From the creative mind behind The Box King and With Stars Above, Seth brings his engaging storytelling and handcrafted puppetry to two special November mornings.

In Dream of Owls, little Theo drifts off to sleep and becomes frightened by a mysterious hooting sound. With guidance from his father and a strangely familiar dream dragon, Theo learns to face his fears by discovering the source of the sound: an owl. Through creativity, curiosity, and knowledge, Theo discovers that understanding the unknown can transform fear into wonder. Families will enjoy a magical puppet experience featuring table-top, hand, and rod puppets as well as an imaginative dream world brought to life through changing sets and colorful transformations. Developed with professional naturalists and environmental educators from Silverwood Park and the Minnesota Zoo, Dream of Owls combines accurate science with engaging storytelling for family audiences.

Seth combines puppetry with environmental education as a teaching artist at Silverwood Park and through partnerships with local schools. His work has been supported by the Minnesota State Arts Board and recognized throughout the regional arts community.

event.title: Advanced Band Weaving Workshop with Kerstin Neumüller
event.description:
This course takes place online over two days, Sat, Nov 21, and Sun, Nov 22, from 10 am-12 pm CST both sessions.

Join Swedish textile artist and educator Kerstin Neumüller for two online sessions focused on more advanced techniques on a small rigid heddle-style band weaving loom. Suitable for students who have previously practiced repp band weaving on their own or in other classes with Kerstin, this workshop takes the next step to focus on pick-up patterns and other possibilities on these small, versatile looms. Students will start by weaving a band with patterned hearts and then discuss the planning and execution of other pick-up band patterns.

This virtual class is an excellent option for students who want a refresher on more advanced band weaving techniques, have previously worked through basic projects from Kerstin’s book Simple Weave, or have taken an in-person or virtual repp band weaving class with Kerstin previously. During work time, discuss project options for small looms, materials, and weaving band tips. Plan for some additional weaving time on your own between the two sessions to get the most out of this project.

Additional information:

  • This class has some homework between the two sessions.
  • Advanced registration required.
  • Students provide their own materials for this virtual class and should be comfortable warping their small rigid heddle loom ahead of class; please see the full materials list here.

 

Prerequisites:

  • Skill level: Suitable for students with past weaving experience.
  • Ages: Suitable for ages 12+.
  • Virtual class info: This is a live virtual class taught over Zoom. Students need a strong internet connection and a device with video capabilities. To participate in this class, students must have their video on.

event.title: Nordic Book Circle
event.description:
Contemporary Nordic literature is full of diverse literary voices, styles, and genres. This September 2026 through May 2027 the ASI Nordic Book Circle will gather monthly, in-person, to read and discuss a work of Nordic literature in English translation. Our focus this year will be on works of literature written by women authors from across the Nordic world. The works we read will chronologically trace books penned between 1912 and 2020, and include two winners of the Nobel Prize in Literature; authors from the countries of Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Iceland, Greenland; various genres; and a range of topics and perspectives.

If you love to read and discuss literature and would like to expand your appreciation of literature from various parts of the world (the Nordic world in particular), we would love to have you join! Limited to 20 attendees; please register in advance.

2026-2027 Nordic Book Circle titles
September: Kristin Lavransdotter, Book I: The Wreath (1912), by Sigrid Undset, translated from Norwegian by Tiina Nunnally (Penguin Editions, 336 pages), Norway – September 27, 2026

October: The Phantom Carriage (1912), by Selma Lagerlöf, translated from Swedish by Peter Graves (Norvik Press, 124 pages) (Sweden) – October 25, 2026

November: Quicksand (1928) by Nella Larsen (Penguin Classics, 192 pages) (Denmark) – November 22, 2026

December: Kallocain (1940), Karin Boye, translated from Swedish by David McDuff (Penguin Classics, 192 pages) (Sweden) – December 20, 2026

January: Girl Upon Heaven’s Pier (1951), by Eeva-Liisa Manner, translated from Finnish by Terhi Kuusisto (Dalkey Archive Press, 104 pages) (Finland) – January 31, 2027

February: Nothing to be Rescued (1961), by Ásta Sigurðardóttir, translated from Icelandic by Meg Matich (Nordisk Books, 192 pages) Iceland – February 28, 2027

March: Light, Grass, and Letter in April (1962, 1963, 1979), by Inger Christensen, translated from Danish by Susanna Nied (New Directions Publishing, 144 pages) (Denmark) – March 21, 2027

April: Zombieland (2015), by Sørine Steenholdt, translated from Greenlandic to Danish by Niviaq Korneliussen and from Danish to English by Charlotte Barslund (Norvik Press, 150 pages) (Greenland) – April 25, 2027

May: Strega (2020), by Johanna Lykke Holm, translated from Swedish by Saskia Vogel (Riverhead Books, 208 pages) (Sweden) – May 23, 2027

event.title: Nordic Handcraft Workshop: Chip Carved Ornaments with Paul Anderson and Mike Hughes
event.description:
Expand your carving skills in this three-session chip carving workshop led by woodcarvers Paul Anderson and Mike Hughes.

This class takes place over three Wednesday evenings, 6-8:30 pm on December 2, 9, and 16.

 

Explore the technique of chip carving in the Scandinavian style. Chip carving is an old and useful form of decoration for woodenware of all kinds, including bowls, plates, spoons, and decorative boxes or signs. It is also perfect for making a beautiful and unique heirloom ornament. In this three-session workshop, students will work alongside woodcarvers Paul Anderson and Mike Hughes to learn basic chip carving techniques and then decorate a small wooden ornament. Basic chip carving techniques, such as tool options and care, wood and pattern selection, and finishing projects, will also be covered as time allows. Students will leave with the skills to practice chip carving more at home, along with an ornament perfect for displaying on a Christmas tree or giving as a special gift.

Additional information:

  • Advanced registration required.
  • A $15 materials fee is due to the instructors in class. Students are invited provide their own chip carving knife (suggested style: Pfeil Swiss chip carving knife #2) and bring a leather strop for sharpening in class if they have them; the instructors also have tools to lend.

 

Prerequisites

  • Physical ability: Please note, carving requires some hand strength and flexibility.
  • Skill level: Open to all skill levels.
  • Ages: Suitable for ages 18+.

event.title: December Open Nordic Jam
event.description:
Join us on the first Thursday of every month for Open Nordic Jam!

Have you ever wanted to play music in the historic Turnblad Mansion? Now’s your chance! Bring your nyckelharpa, hardingfele, fiddle, or any acoustic instrument to ASI’s Open Nordic Jam. This jam is open to musicians of all levels who want to learn and play Nordic folk music. Bring your friends or plan to make new ones here!

Minnesota has long been known for its rich music scenes—in part due to the many immigrant diasporas that have established themselves in the area. From Nisswa-stämman to the Nordic Roots festival, to the countless house jams across the state, Nordic folk music is an important part of Minnesota’s musical identity. Whether you’re a master fiddler or want to learn more about folk music, this monthly gathering is for you!

This jam is facilitated by ASI staff, but tunes are selected each time by musicians in the room. We will play standards and originals inspired by the folk traditions of Sweden, Norway, Finland, Denmark, and Iceland. While many musicians may bring traditional instruments, all acoustic instrumentalists are welcome to participate. If you do not play an instrument, you can still attend if you respectfully observe and listen. Dancing is encouraged but not required—see you there! No advanced registration required.

event.title: Nordic Table Demo: Glögg Party with Kristi Bissell
event.description:
Join Kristi Bissell for a virtual demo on celebrating a Glögg Party.

Celebrate the season Swedish style with a glöggmingle or Mulled Wine Party! Kristi Bissell of True North Kitchen will share some of her favorite seasonal recipes, including her take on Swedish mulled wine or glögg, a trio of mini open-faced sandwiches, and a Pear Cardamom Cake. Whether you are inspired to host a feast or incorporate these recipes into other seasonal meals, you’ll be set with great options for savory and sweet nibbles throughout the holidays.

Additional information:

  • This class is designed as a demonstration so students can watch the entire process and ask questions before tackling the recipe at home later.
  • The recipe packet will be shared via email and available for download one week in advance.

Virtual class information:

  • This live virtual class, taught over Zoom, includes access to the class recording for one month after the class; registrants may attend live or watch the recording at their convenience during that time.
  • Students need a strong internet connection and a device with video capabilities. Advanced registration required.

event.title: Nordic Table Demo: A Jolly Troll Julbord with Patrice Johnson and Carole Jean Anderson
event.description:
Join Patrice Johnson and Carole Jean Anderson for an evening workshop celebrating the Minnesota restaurant Jolly Troll. 

Come for the trolls, stay for the julbord! This holiday season, the much-missed Minnesota restaurant Jolly Troll is featured in ASI’s annual holiday experience, and this evening class gives guests a special peek back into the magic of this beloved restaurant. Visit the trolls in the holiday exhibition, then join Carole Jean Anderson and Patrice Johnson for this evening demonstration featuring some favorite recipes from the Jolly Troll menus. Carole Jean will share memories (and maybe a few songs) from her life in the Jolly Troll restaurant family, and Patrice will cook up an assortment of holiday treats, from cranberry fluff to meatballs to rice pudding.

Additional information:

  • This class includes a light meal. Coffee and tea provided; additional beverages are available for purchase prior to class.
  • Please confirm dietary restrictions with ASI upon registration.
  • Advanced registration required.
event.excerpt: Delicately spiced meatballs are a hallmark of Swedish Christmas tables—make sure you have recipes up your sleeve that can be adapted for all guests!

event.title: Craft and Cocktails Workshop: Carve and Paint a Ceramic Ornament with Kim Burnham
event.description:
ASI’s Craft and Cocktails workshops are fun and approachable sessions in community. Join potter Kim Burnham to carve and paint a ceramic ornament.

Join potter Kim Burnham of ImoKim Pottery to try out decorating a ceramic ornament with the sgrafitto technique while enjoying a beverage from FIKA Café! Students will learn the basics of adding a design to ceramics by carving and painting on a round 3.5″ greenware ornament base. Use a template provided by the instructor or bring ideas for your own design! The ornaments will be glazed with a top clear coat and then fired before returning to ASI for pick up a few weeks after class. One beverage from FIKA is included in the class fee.

Additional information:

  • Advanced registration required.
  • A $25 materials fee is paid to the instructor in class and covers all tools and materials.
  • A beverage from FIKA Café is included in the class fee.
  • Fired ornaments will be returned to ASI for pickup a few weeks after class.

 

Prerequisites:

  • Skill level: Open to all skill levels.
  • Ages: Craft and Cocktails programs are suitable for ages 21+.
event.excerpt: ASI’s Craft and Cocktails workshops are fun and approachable sessions in community. Join potter Kim Burnham to carve and paint a ceramic ornament.

event.title: Babies at the Castle
event.description:
Share Swedish art and culture with your baby during a morning of exploration at the Turnblad Mansion.

Caregivers and infants up to 18 months are invited to experience ASI’s annual holiday experience, Remember When, in the historic Turnblad Mansion. During this special tour, babies and their caregivers explore festive displays, discover stories from the past, and engage with the sights, sounds, and details of the holiday season together. Through close looking, shared attention, and simple activities, families build meaningful connections with art, history, and each other.

ASI educator Jason Leuthold guides caregivers and babies through each stop, offering age-appropriate activities that encourage curiosity, exploration, and engagement. Caregivers carry infants at eye level, allowing babies to experience artwork and installations up close while supporting early visual exploration and shared discovery. Each 30-minute tour offers a unique experience and concludes with 15 minutes of sensory play in the Castle before it opens to the public at 10 am.

Additional Information:

  • Admission is included with registration, allowing participants to explore the current exhibition and Family Gallery after the program.
  • Advanced registration is required. Please register by the Friday before the program. ASI may cancel the program if registration is low.
  • Strollers are not permitted in exhibition spaces.
  • ASI educators encourage caregivers to carry infants so babies can view artwork and installations at eye level.
  • Food, beverages, and chewing gum are not permitted in exhibition spaces.
event.excerpt: Caregivers and infants experience ASI’s holiday exhibition through guided exploration, sensory play, and hands-on activities together

event.title: Preschool Program: Lucia’s Legend
event.description:
ASI’s Preschool Program creates opportunities for families to experience Swedish art, culture, and traditions together. Join us in December to explore the legend of Saint Lucia.

Families with preschoolers are invited to explore what “Swedish Christmas” means through Lucia’s Legend at the American Swedish Institute. This hands-on program introduces children and their grown-ups to the legend of Sankta Lucia through stories, music, and crafts.

Together, preschoolers and their important grown-ups discover the traditions behind Lucia Day by exploring questions like, “What do Swedish families do on Lucia Day?” and “Why do they do it?” Preschoolers will go home with their own Lucia Crown or Star Boy wand, recipes, and ideas for creating their own Lucia celebration at home. ASI’s Lucia Choir Director, Ingrid Aune, co-teaches this program with ASI Educator Lindsey Tscherne, guiding preschoolers through an engaging introduction to this beloved Swedish tradition.

Additional Information:

  • This program is designed specifically for children ages 3-5 and their important grown-ups.
  • Museum admission is included with registration.
  • Adult accompaniment is required.
  • Adult admission is included with child registration.
  • The program limits attendance to one adult per registered preschooler.
  • Please arrive 15 minutes early so the program can begin promptly at 10 am.
  • Register by December 4.

Make your own line of festive gift wrap this holiday season! Jeanne will share inspiration for how simple forms can be combined and repeated for making impactful designs. Students will sketch a few designs, transferring them to rubber, and carve one or more small stamps. Finally, students will have the opportunity to print some gift tags, bags and paper for wrapping. Students will leave with their stamps and the tools to make even more gift-wrapping materials at home.

Additional information:

  • Advanced registration required.
  • A $40 materials fee is payable to the instructor in class and covers stamp carving materials and some assorted gift wrap options.
  • Students get to take their stamps and stamp making tools home.

  • Skill level: Open to all skill levels.
  • Ages: Suitable for ages 18+.

The ASI Lucia Choir and Lilla Lag bring this magical one-hour concert to life through songs that celebrate hope, light, and community. Set in the beautiful Larson Hall, this annual tradition invites audiences of all ages to experience the beauty and joy of Swedish holiday music.

FIKA Café will serve a special festival menu with small plates and warm glögg (Swedish mulled wine). The ASI Museum Store and Jul Shop will also be open late for all your last-minute gift needs!

Cozy bonfires, warm hot chocolate, light snowfall, and comforting tunes blend to make the most mysig experience possible. In true Minnesota fashion, this event is always held both indoors and outdoors (with hot chocolate and glögg, of course), featuring activities like kick sledding to enjoy the winter to its fullest.

event.title: Nordic Handcraft Workshop: Carve a Heart with Maeve Gathje
event.description:
Join carving instructor Maeve Gathje in a half-day flat plane carving workshop to create a wooden heart decoration.

Try your hand at carving by making a sweet wooden heart decoration with carving instructor Maeve. This beginner-level course will introduce students to the tradition of Scandinavian-style flat plane carving, including basic knife grips and carving techniques. Related topics such as acquiring and preparing tools and materials will be covered throughout the class. The finished hearts will be perfect for display during the holidays, gifting, or even making a statement necklace.

Additional information:

  • Advanced registration required.
  • A $10 materials fee is payable to the instructor in class.

event.title: Nordic Handcraft Workshop: Flat Plane Carved Ornaments with Maeve Gathje
event.description:
Join carving instructor Maeve Gathje in a full-day workshop focused on transforming pre-cut shapes into carved ornaments.

Try your hand at carving while creating unique wooden ornaments to spruce up your holiday tree. This beginner-level carving course with Maeve Gathje will introduce students to the tradition of Scandinavian-style flat plane carving, including basic knife grips and carving techniques. Students will choose from a selection of pre-cut shapes and use a carving knife to add details and character to each design. Students should expect to take home four ornaments that can be painted or oiled after class, and then displayed or gifted. This class is the perfect way to connect with family over the holidays and maybe even start a new tradition.

Additional information:

  • Advanced registration required.
  • A $20 materials fee is paid to the instructor in class and covers all tools and materials.
  • Finishing options such as painting or oiling will also be discussed in class.

 

Prerequisites:

  • Physical ability: Some experience with woodcarving (such as previous short ASI woodcarving class) is suggested but not required. Woodcarving requires good hand strength and flexibility.
  • Skill level: Open to all skill levels.
  • Ages: Suitable for ages 16+, or ages 11-15 welcome to register alongside an accompanying adult.
event.excerpt: Try your hand at carving while creating unique wooden ornaments using Scandinavian-style flat plane carving. Ages 16+ or 11-15 alongside an adult.

event.title: Nordic Handcraft Workshop: Felted Globe Luminaries with Judy McDowell
event.description:
Learn from felting instructor Judy McDowell to create felted wool luminaries in this hands-on 5-hour workshop.

Celebrate the return of light after the Winter Solstice by creating felted wool luminaries, which bring a cozy glow even after the holiday season. Using traditional wet felting techniques, students will work alongside felting instructor Judy McDowell to lay out wool in thin layers around a pattern, add soapy water, and roll, rub, and manipulate the wool into a perfect light-weight woolen globe that can be lit from within with a candle or string lights. Students can expect to leave the class with one to two finished luminaries, depending on size.

Tools and Materials:

  • A materials fee of about $20-$30 is payable to the instructor, depending on the size of the projects chosen.
  • Students are also encouraged to bring 2-3 old bath towels, a bag to take home wet projects in, and an apron.

 

Prerequisites:

  • Advanced registration required.
  • Physical ability: This workshop requires hand strength and some extended standing.
  • Skill level: Open to all skill levels.
  • Ages: Suitable for ages 16+. A discounted price for youth is available at checkout.
event.excerpt: Use wet felting techniques to make a felted wool globe luminary, which can be illuminated from within to bring a cozy glow to your home. Ages 16+

event.title: Nordic Book Circle
event.description:
Contemporary Nordic literature is full of diverse literary voices, styles, and genres. This September 2026 through May 2027 the ASI Nordic Book Circle will gather monthly, in-person, to read and discuss a work of Nordic literature in English translation. Our focus this year will be on works of literature written by women authors from across the Nordic world. The works we read will chronologically trace books penned between 1912 and 2020, and include two winners of the Nobel Prize in Literature; authors from the countries of Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Iceland, Greenland; various genres; and a range of topics and perspectives.

event.description:

Try out Scandinavian-style woodcarving in this one-day hands on workshop. Students will work with fresh “green” wood, a carving knife, and a few other simple hand tools to make some simple kitchen tools. Starting with the basic knife grips, each student will carve a spreader for butter, jam, or soft cheeses, then move on to using a drawknife and shaving horse to create a simple spatula. This is a terrific introduction to foundational hand tools and techniques that will take students on to spoons, bowls, and lots of other interesting projects!

event.description:
Join carving instructor Maeve Gathje in a full-day workshop focused on honing carving skills to carve sculpted figures.

Jump into the world of Scandinavian-style flat plane carving in this one-day class, focused on carving “tiny folk” or small characters. Maeve Gathje will get students started with the technique of carving faces and people “on the corner” of a rectangular block. This simple format is easy to get started with and still offers lots of great practice for new carvers to practice knife skills and exercise their creativity. In the morning, students will start on their two 1″ x 1″ x 3″ figures, about the size of a standard chess piece, with a focus on the cuts that define faces. In the afternoon, students will paint their characters using milk paint. Throughout the day, tool and material selection, knife safety techniques, and finishing options will all be discussed. Students will go home ready to carve a whole village of characters!

Additional information:

  • Advanced registration required.
  • A $40 is due to instructor Maeve Gathje in class and covers all required tools, wood and milk paint for at least two 1″ x 1″x 3″ figures.

event.title: January Open Nordic Jam
event.description:
Join us on the first Thursday of every month for Open Nordic Jam!

Have you ever wanted to play music in the historic Turnblad Mansion? Now’s your chance! Bring your nyckelharpa, hardingfele, fiddle, or any acoustic instrument to ASI’s Open Nordic Jam. This jam is open to musicians of all levels who want to learn and play Nordic folk music. Bring your friends or plan to make new ones here!

Minnesota has long been known for its rich music scenes—in part due to the many immigrant diasporas that have established themselves in the area. From Nisswa-stämman to the Nordic Roots festival, to the countless house jams across the state, Nordic folk music is an important part of Minnesota’s musical identity. Whether you’re a master fiddler or want to learn more about folk music, this monthly gathering is for you!

This jam is facilitated by ASI staff, but tunes are selected each time by musicians in the room. We will play standards and originals inspired by the folk traditions of Sweden, Norway, Finland, Denmark, and Iceland. While many musicians may bring traditional instruments, all acoustic instrumentalists are welcome to participate. If you do not play an instrument, you can still attend if you respectfully observe and listen. Dancing is encouraged but not required—see you there! No advanced registration required.

event.title: Nordic Handcraft Workshop: Intro to Card Weaving Workshop with Josie Cooke
event.description:
Explore the art of card weaving with instructor Josie Cooke in this full-day workshop.

Card weaving is an extremely old and important band weaving technique, commonly used in Scandinavia to create beautifully patterned bands for edging textiles or using as apron strings or belts. While in the early Iron Age, card woven bands were used to create the starting and selvedge bands for warp weighted looms, today those same bands might be put to use as decorative edging on a sweater, as straps for a bag, or as a stylish lanyard for glasses or keys. In this one-day workshop, students will choose from a variety of patterns and weave a band approximately 3/8″- 3/4″ wide and 24″-36″ long. At the end of the day, students will leave with a set of cards and the skills to continue band weaving beyond class.

Additional information:

  • Advanced registration required.
  • A $25 materials fee is due in class to the instructor.
  • Students receive a set of cards to take home.

event.title: Bring new life to old family archives – Chris Fischbach
event.description:
Join former Coffee House Press publisher and current literary agent Chris Fischbach as he leads a laid-back three-hour workshop exploring different creative activities you can do with your family archives.

Do you have boxes of old family journals, letters, photographs, records, and receipts from multiple generations of relatives, but not know what to do with them? Why not use these “family archives” as inspiration, material, and jumping-off points for creativity?

Come to class with a general idea of what your archives contain, such as old family journals, letters, photos, maps, documents like marriage licenses and birth certificates, shopping lists, keepsakes, ticket stubs, travel documents, passports, etc. You don’t need to bring any of this with you, but you are welcome to. Please bring a notebook and something to write with. You will leave the class with ideas for new ways to discover, create, and make something new from something old. You will also have something your family can cherish for years to come. Bring the past to life and make your ancestors proud as their archives inspire you to create, tell their story in words or collage, tell it slant, or create a different world with them as characters.

As we prepare and share a light meal, we’ll explore the central tenets of New Nordic cuisine, including seasonality and locally sourced ingredients, and their applications to today’s Midwestern tables. We’ll also touch on how the environment, migration, and trade have both changed and preserved food traditions in both Scandinavia and Scandinavian-American communities over the past 150 years. Our menu and discussion will share just how diverse, colorful, and nutritious the Nordic Table can be!

Additional information:

  • This is a demonstration-style class and includes a light meal.
  • Coffee and tea are provided; additional beverages are available for purchase before class.
  • Please note this menu contains fish, pork, gluten, and dairy (with a vegan main dish available), so please reach out if you have questions about dietary accommodations.
  • Advanced registration required.
event.excerpt: Join Patrice for an introduction to ASI’s Nordic Table program in this demo class. Prepare and share a light meal and explore New Nordic cuisine.

event.title: Swedish Grammar Intensive: Morphology – Rachel Willson-Broyles
event.description:
Dive deep into Swedish grammar and morphology with Rachel Willson-Broyles.

Do you love going down the rabbit hole of grammar? Or perhaps grammar confuses you, but you want to understand it better. Join us! This class, taught by Rachel Willson-Broyles, will introduce the grammar topic of morphology with examples and handouts, and you can expect some in-class exercises and group work. Grammar terms will also be introduced and explained. In linguistics, morphology is the study of words, and there are many intriguing aspects of word-building in Swedish to explore. In this class, we will discuss compound words and their formation as well as prefixes (such as o-) and suffixes (such as -ig) and how they work.

Additional information:

  • This grammar intensive is appropriate for intermediate students and higher (i.e., your regular class is using the B1/B2 textbook).
  • Advanced registration required.
event.excerpt: Dive deep into Swedish grammar and morphology with Rachel Willson-Broyles.

Grab a friend and enjoy a beverage from FIKA Café while making a sweet woolly scene. Using a felt base, colorful wool, and felting needles, students will use needle felting techniques to “paint with wool” to create a colorful scene. The finished scenes will be fixed inside a mini grapevine wreath, perfect for display. No previous experience is necessary to head home with a beautiful decoration that captures the best of winter!

event.title: Nordic Handcraft Workshop: Painting with Swedish Egg Yolk Paint with Pieper Fleck Bloomquist
event.description:
Learn to make your own natural paint out of egg yolks in the style of folk paints from Southern Sweden!

Historically, paints were mixed from many different easily accessible bases, including egg yolks. In this intro level class, students will work alongside contemporary folk artist Pieper Bloomquist to mix multiple colors of paints and use them to paint some typical flowers found in older folk paintings in Southern Sweden.

Finally, students may also wish to wear an apron or otherwise wear clothes that can get a little messy.

 

Prerequisites:

  • Skill level: This program is appropriate for all skill levels.

event.title: Nordic Handcraft Workshop: Swedish Kurbits (Dalmålning) Painting with Pieper Fleck Bloomquist
event.description:
This class meets for two days Saturday–Sunday, January 16–17, from 10 am–5 pm both days.

Explore the art of kurbits in this weekend long Swedish folk painting class.

Discover the colorful world of the kurbits in this fun, weekend-long Swedish folk painting workshop inspired by the decorated farmhouses of Dalarna, Sweden. Students will learn to paint the iconic “kurbit” motif of flowing flowers, leaves, and whimsical designs that made this folk tradition famous. Alongside painting, the class will discuss the history of dalmålning and its deep connection to Swedish heritage.

Using acrylics on canvas, each student will practice simple traditional motifs and techniques that easily translate to watercolor, markers, oils, and more. Templates and patterns are available for anyone who wants extra guidance, making this class welcoming and enjoyable for all skill levels.

Tools and Materials:

  • A $20 materials fee paid to the instructor covers all necessary supplies.
  • Students are additionally invited to bring their favorite supplies for acrylic painting such as brushes, water pans, wet palette, and/or a sketchbook. Recommended brush sizes include #2, #4, and #6 round, and #3/0, #1 liner.
  • An introductory video will be provided and should be watched before class.

 

Prerequisites:

  • Advanced registration required.
  • Ages: Suitable for ages 14+. A discounted ticket price for students ages 14-17 is available at checkout.
  • Skill level: This class is suitable for all experience levels.

event.title: Pippi’s After Christmas Party
event.description:
Celebrate the Swedish tradition of julgransplundring to give the holiday season one final burst of music, laughter, and togetherness. This playful celebration is inspired by Astrid Lindgren’s beloved Pippi Longstocking stories.

This program will go on sale Monday, September 28 (ASI members) and Friday, October 2 (public).

Pippi’s After Christmas Party invites children and their important grown ups to celebrate julgransplundring, a beloved Swedish tradition that gives the holiday season one final burst of music, laughter, and togetherness. In Sweden, julgransplundring marks the end of the Christmas season, when families and friends gather one last time to enjoy the Christmas tree before putting away the holiday decorations. At ASI, all ages can discover this joyful tradition and send the season off with one last celebration as the Christmas tree comes down.

Inspired by Astrid Lindgren’s beloved Pippi Longstocking stories, this playful celebration brings the spirit of Villa Villekulla to ASI. Pippi Longstocking herself will join the celebration, giving participants the opportunity to interact with Pippi, embrace her playful spirit, and create cheerful memories together.

ASI educators and Ross Sutter will lead an afternoon filled with creativity, crafts, music, movement, and holiday fun. Children and their important grown ups can make decorations, dance around the Christmas trees, play, and enjoy one final burst of holiday joy together.

Additional information:

  • This program welcomes children and their important grown-ups of all ages.
  • Food and beverages are available for purchase at FIKA Cafe and may be enjoyed during the program.
  • Museum admission is included with registration, allowing participants to continue exploring ASI after the program.
event.excerpt: Discover the Swedish tradition of julgransplundring with Pippi’s After Christmas Party, a joyful celebration of music, creativity, and togetherness.

event.title: Nordic Table Demo: Beyond Bread – Cooking and Baking with Rye with Kristi Bissell
event.description:
Learn how to use rye, an important ingredient in the Nordic Kitchen, in cookies, cakes, and savory dishes with Kristi Bissell.

Rye is a staple ingredient in the Nordic kitchen, most often on the table as dense, hearty rye bread or thin, versatile crispbread. But Kristi Bissell of the blog True North Kitchen is ready to stretch our imaginations beyond just bread! Sourcing and using rye berries and flour deserve a little extra attention, and Kristi will discuss her tips and tricks for using rye while walking students through recipes for a cookie, a cake, and a savory dish in this hour-long demo.

event.title: Skinnfell – The Printed Sheepskin Workshop with Becky Utecht and Sue Flanders
event.description:
Learn about the history of Norwegian Skinnfell, embellished sheepskins, while block printing and finishing a tanned sheepskin with instructors Becky Utecht and Sue Flanders.

Join Becky Utecht and Sue Flanders for a day long introduction to the Norwegian art of skinnfell, an embellished sheepskin. Skinnfell are sheepskins with stitched and finished edges, printed with wood block stamps. They are often sewn together into a warm coverlet, but in this introductory class we will use one sheepskin to create a chair pad, bench cover, or wall hanging. Students will learn about the history of this unique craft while cutting, printing and finishing a provided tanned sheepskin to create a finished piece of about 22″ by 32″. Special attention will be given to the use of the instructors’ Norwegian print blocks and the symbolism of different patterns meant to bring good will to the user. Students will apply a “bridal” edging, which will be completed after class. This class offers a broad overview to this unique craft, which can be applied in many decorative and useful applications for future projects.

Prerequisites:

  • Advanced registration required.
  • Ages: This workshop welcomes students 16+. A discounted tuition is available for students ages 16-17 at checkout.
  • Skill level: This workshop is open to all experience levels.
  • Physical: Please note that to complete this project, students need good hand strength and flexibility, as sewing leather is difficult hand work.

 

Tools and Materials:

  • A $115 materials fee covers one full sized tanned sheepskin, use of the print blocks and paint, and other necessary supplies.
  • Students are also encouraged to bring the following tools if possible: a large, clear plastic quilting ruler; a small pair of very sharp scissors; several sturdy metal clips; a leather thimble; and a small jewelry pliers.

event.title: How Sweden Works: Democracy and the Right to Vote – Alexander Fooy
event.description: In a relatively short space of time between the end of the 19th century to the early-mid 20th century, Sweden went from a state of near-absolute monarchy to a widely recognized bastion of social democracy… how did that happen? From the Garden Crisis of 1914 to the clarification of the People’s Home welfare state ideology in 1928, and the adoption of the modern Swedish constitution in 1974, this lecture by Alexander Fooy will cover the development of the modern Swedish political system and how the currents driving modern Swedish politics have their roots in these now long-ago social trends. Advanced registration required.

event.title: Nordic Book Circle
event.description:
Contemporary Nordic literature is full of diverse literary voices, styles, and genres. This September 2026 through May 2027 the ASI Nordic Book Circle will gather monthly, in-person, to read and discuss a work of Nordic literature in English translation. Our focus this year will be on works of literature written by women authors from across the Nordic world. The works we read will chronologically trace books penned between 1912 and 2020, and include two winners of the Nobel Prize in Literature; authors from the countries of Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Iceland, Greenland; various genres; and a range of topics and perspectives.

If you love to read and discuss literature and would like to expand your appreciation of literature from various parts of the world (the Nordic world in particular), we would love to have you join! Limited to 20 attendees; please register in advance.

event.title: February Open Nordic Jam
event.description:
Join us on the first Thursday of every month for Open Nordic Jam!

Have you ever wanted to play music in the historic Turnblad Mansion? Now’s your chance! Bring your nyckelharpa, hardingfele, fiddle, or any acoustic instrument to ASI’s Open Nordic Jam. This jam is open to musicians of all levels who want to learn and play Nordic folk music. Bring your friends or plan to make new ones here!

Minnesota has long been known for its rich music scenes—in part due to the many immigrant diasporas that have established themselves in the area. From Nisswa-stämman to the Nordic Roots festival, to the countless house jams across the state, Nordic folk music is an important part of Minnesota’s musical identity. Whether you’re a master fiddler or want to learn more about folk music, this monthly gathering is for you!

This jam is facilitated by ASI staff, but tunes are selected each time by musicians in the room. We will play standards and originals inspired by the folk traditions of Sweden, Norway, Finland, Denmark, and Iceland. While many musicians may bring traditional instruments, all acoustic instrumentalists are welcome to participate. If you do not play an instrument, you can still attend if you respectfully observe and listen. Dancing is encouraged but not required—see you there! No advanced registration required.

event.title: Nordic Handcraft Workshop: Dried Florals Wreath with Elle Sullivan
event.description:
Create a stunning dried flower wreath for the winter season with instructor Elle Sullivan in this two-hour evening workshop.

Bring a little color to your home this winter in this floral wreath workshop with farmer-florist Elle Sullivan of Mellifera Flowers! Using vibrant dried flowers, leaves, and grasses, students will build hand-tied wreath from preserved elements of last year’s harvest. The workshop will begin with a discussion of color theory and other design principles to consider for wreath-making, and Elle will demo the tips and tricks she’s cultivated over the years for making a balanced and personality-filled wreath. Students will finish the workshop with a long lasting completed wreath made on a 10″ base.

Additional information:

  • Advanced registration required.
  • A $50 materials fee is due in class to the instructor and covers all materials to make a 10″ wreath.
  • This workshop is suitable for students 18+.
  • No previous experience necessary.

event.title: Nordic Handcraft Workshop: Binding a Hardcover Book with Maeve Gathje
event.description:
Get started with bookbinding while creating a hardcover book just the size and colors you need.

This class meets Saturday, February 6 and Sunday, February 7, 9 am-4 pm both days.

A handmade hardcover book can record anything from journal entries to sketches, recipes to guest remembrances. This class focuses on a style of codex bookbinding (i.e., folded pages attached to a binding) with a sewn text block, resulting in a strong and firm set of pages inside a book cloth-wrapped hardcover. Working alongside instructor Maeve Gathje, students will complete all the steps of binding at least one book, and begin or even complete at least one more, as well as leave with the skills and tools to continue binding books beyond the course. Throughout the class, Maeve will address various tools, alternative techniques, design elements, problem-solving strategies, and questions about future adventures in bookbinding.

 

Prerequisites:

  • Advanced registration required.
  • Skill level: Open to all skill levels.
  • Ages: Suitable for ages 18+.

 

Tools and Materials:

  • An $85 materials fee is due in class to the instructor and includes materials and tool use for at least two books.
  • Books need to be pressed overnight after binding, and students have several options: they may provide their own book press (at least 8″ x 14″ and fits books up to 2″ deep) or purchase one from the instructor for $45, which allows them to take their books home on the last night of class. Alternatively, students may leave their books pressing overnight at ASI and pick up their finished books later in the week for no additional charge.
event.excerpt: Get started with bookbinding while making two unique hardcover books just the size (and colors) you need. Suitable for ages 18+.

event.title: Preschool Program: Alla Hjärtans Dag
event.description:
ASI’s Preschool Program creates opportunities for families to experience Swedish art, culture, and traditions together. Join us in February to explore Alla Hjärtans Dag.

Preschoolers and their important grown-ups discover how Swedish families celebrate Alla Hjärtans Dag, or “All Hearts’ Day,” during this special morning at ASI. Through stories, crafts, and hands-on activities, children explore how people in Sweden use this day to show care and appreciation for the people they love. Together, preschoolers and their important grown-ups explore questions like, “How do Swedish families celebrate Alla Hjärtans Dag?” and “Why do they celebrate it?”

Children will create a special craft, taste Swedish candy, and explore the Castle while discovering the traditions behind this heartwarming holiday. ASI educators guide preschoolers and their important grown-ups through a playful introduction to Swedish culture, encouraging curiosity, creativity, and connection. Participants leave with new ideas for celebrating kindness and togetherness at home.

Additional information:

  • This program is designed specifically for children ages 3–5 and their important grown-ups.
  • Museum admission is included with registration.
  • Adult admission is included with child registration.
  • Adult accompaniment is required.
  • The program limits attendance to one adult per registered preschooler.
  • Please arrive 15 minutes early so the program can begin promptly at 10 am.
  • Register by Friday, February 5.
  • ASI may cancel the program due to low registration.

event.title: Nordic Book Circle
event.description:
Contemporary Nordic literature is full of diverse literary voices, styles, and genres. This September 2026 through May 2027 the ASI Nordic Book Circle will gather monthly, in-person, to read and discuss a work of Nordic literature in English translation. Our focus this year will be on works of literature written by women authors from across the Nordic world. The works we read will chronologically trace books penned between 1912 and 2020, and include two winners of the Nobel Prize in Literature; authors from the countries of Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Iceland, Greenland; various genres; and a range of topics and perspectives.

If you love to read and discuss literature and would like to expand your appreciation of literature from various parts of the world (the Nordic world in particular), we would love to have you join! Limited to 20 attendees; please register in advance.

2026-2027 Nordic Book Circle titles
September: Kristin Lavransdotter, Book I: The Wreath (1912), by Sigrid Undset, translated from Norwegian by Tiina Nunnally (Penguin Editions, 336 pages), Norway – September 27, 2026

October: The Phantom Carriage (1912), by Selma Lagerlöf, translated from Swedish by Peter Graves (Norvik Press, 124 pages) (Sweden) – October 25, 2026

November: Quicksand (1928) by Nella Larsen (Penguin Classics, 192 pages) (Denmark) – November 22, 2026

December: Kallocain (1940), Karin Boye, translated from Swedish by David McDuff (Penguin Classics, 192 pages) (Sweden) – December 20, 2026

January: Girl Upon Heaven’s Pier (1951), by Eeva-Liisa Manner, translated from Finnish by Terhi Kuusisto (Dalkey Archive Press, 104 pages) (Finland) – January 31, 2027

February: Nothing to be Rescued (1961), by Ásta Sigurðardóttir, translated from Icelandic by Meg Matich (Nordisk Books, 192 pages) Iceland – February 28, 2027

March: Light, Grass, and Letter in April (1962, 1963, 1979), by Inger Christensen, translated from Danish by Susanna Nied (New Directions Publishing, 144 pages) (Denmark) – March 21, 2027

April: Zombieland (2015), by Sørine Steenholdt, translated from Greenlandic to Danish by Niviaq Korneliussen and from Danish to English by Charlotte Barslund (Norvik Press, 150 pages) (Greenland) – April 25, 2027

May: Strega (2020), by Johanna Lykke Holm, translated from Swedish by Saskia Vogel (Riverhead Books, 208 pages) (Sweden) – May 23, 2027

event.title: FIKA Supper Club Concert Series: Wingra Wind Quintet
event.description:
Dive deeper into the world of Nordic classical music with University of Wisconsin-Madison’s faculty ensemble, Wingra Wind Quintet. This group featuring flute, oboe, clarinet, horn and bassoon will present works by Nordic composers. Founded in 1965, the Wingra Wind Quintet is one of the longest-running quintets in the nation. Known for artistic and pedagogical excellence, the ensemble has consistently presented concerts and workshops around the globe to rave reviews.

The FIKA Supper Club series brings Nordic-inflected folk, jazz and classical artists to ASI. Optionally, guests may enjoy extended dinner hours at FIKA Café before the concert, then step into Larson Hall for a musical treat beginning at 7 pm. Don’t miss these nights of musical and culinary delight!

Additional information:

  • Limited dinner reservations and a cash bar are available from 4-7 pm. To reserve your table, email fika@asimn.org.
  • Advanced registration recommended. If available, tickets at the door will increase to $40.
  • NEW this season: purchase a FIKA Supper Club Season Package for $175 ($150 ASI member). Join us for 6 terrific Nordic-inflected folk, jazz, and classical music concerts for the price of 5! This option is available at checkout through October 16.

Under the auspices of Kalmar Läns Musikstiftelse, the ensemble has garnered a reputation for its distinctive performance style, captivating audiences with standing performances, a conductor-less approach, and occasional reliance on memory rather than scores. Comprised of both permanent and international members, Camerata Nordica draws exceptional talent from chamber music ensembles and orchestras across Sweden and Europe. Don’t miss this special performance!

event.title: Nordic Book Circle

Step back in time with an exclusive Unseen Missoula historic walking tour. Discover hidden stories as you wander the streets of Downtown with expert guides. Then, enjoy a curated fine dining experience that beautifully blends history and flavor. It’s not just a meal – it’s a journey through time, with the opportunity to connect with your community and support what you love about Downtown.

Connect with fellow supporters and learn about the Missoula Downtown Foundation’s latest projects and initiatives. Hotels and Hooligans Tour

Daily life and culture in Missoula during the city’s railroad boom—the Hotels and Hooligans tour looks at how the average Missoulian (whether long-time or just passing through) lived and recreated. Scandals and other sketchiness from the Courthouse to the seedy underbelly of Missoula’s railroad hotel district will also be revealed!

event.title: Navigating the Genderverse Workshop
event.description:
Navigating the Genderverse Workshop | TransVisible Montana

This presentation is created and facilitated by TransVisible Montana collective members with the intention of creating a “brave space” for folks to gain education regarding the challenges that misinformation and cisnormative systems create for transgender, non-binary, and Two-Spirit Montanans.

Participants will learn what support is helpful in overcoming challenges and will be engaged in activities and discussions that deepen their understanding and comfort with pronouns and their use in introductions.

Participants will explore gender as a part of the human experience that expands beyond the gender binary, and identify effective and ineffective allyship qualities.

Participants will have the opportunity to collect TransVisible Montana resources such as posters, stickers, cards, and handouts that will be helpful in the continued practice of their newly acquired knowledge and allyship skills.

Outcomes Include:

  • A broadened awareness & practice of contemporary, inclusive language.
  • Applicable skills & ideas for work, home, school & public environments.
  • Permission for liberation from the gender binary!

Towards the end of the event, there will be an opportunity to make a meaningful donation that will directly support the enhancement of Downtown through the vibrancy of arts and culture, livability, economy, and safety.

Bricks and Brothels Historic Tour

While most in Missoula are familiar with the name Mary Gleim or the brief history of Front Street, many of the district’s stories remain untold including Gleim’s and her businesses. Since its existence along the historic Mullan Road, Front Street has been dubbed with the title of Missoula’s ‘red light district’ implicating that district remained a place of vice, sin, and corruption influenced by the radical reformist religious movements of the late 19th century. However, violence and addiction found throughout the entirety of the American West remain only a sliver of the true story.

From 1889-1917, West Front and Main Streets became home to a vibrant ‘restricted’ community of working women, Chinese laborers, African American soldiers, and immigrants who built the environment we as Missoulians have come to love today. This tour discusses the district through the historical lenses of sex, race, class, and occupation in order to create a broader social understanding against the backdrop of the remaining built environment.

Join us this and every Tuesday as we compete in a free and friendly game of trivia. Prizes awarded to the top 3 teams.

America’s Pub Quiz is the best live-hosted trivia show that brings a free quiz night to bars, pubs, and restaurants throughout the United States. We are happy to bring fun trivia to family, friends and coworkers. An entertaining evening to be had by all guaranteed. We are so confident in your enjoyment that we aren’t going to charge you anything to play and provide free prizes!

Subject matter is a potpourri of categories, including music, movies, TV, sports, history, and more, with plenty of surprises along the way. A plethora of categories gives all team members their strong subject and ensures the useless knowledge stored away will finally be put to good use. Team size doesn’t matter and there are often prizes for the best team name or funniest wrong answer.

Grab your friends, invite that smart guy from the office, and come take a break with some great food & drink at one of America’s premier establishments. We promise, once you play along with America’s Pub Quiz, you’ll be back!

event.title: Much Ado About Murder
event.description:
By Pat Cook / Rich but rotten Carlton Larraby enjoyed punctuating the lives of his family with macabre little surprises. His latest joke is a Halloween party with everybody dressed as a character from Shakespeare. When the play begins, the bored guests have arrived and wait impatiently for their host to show up, unaware that he has been gruesomely bludgeoned to death in his study. Since this is an audience-participation play, the murder is revealed to the audience before the characters of the play know about it. A sinister master of ceremonies named Mr. Hawker tells the audience what has happened in a series of flashbacks as he lets them see the events surrounding the murder. Little by little, as the audience gets to know the people of the drama, they begin suspecting who the murderer might be … only to discover that they’re wrong. To help them further, Mr. Hawker invites them to view the clue-rich scene of the crime during intermission. Finally, near the end of Act II, he gives the audience the opportunity to question the characters. All the ingredients of a deliciously frightening murder mystery are here—lightning, thunder, weird sounds, screams in the dark—plus the fun of letting the audience participate in solving the crime. As a critic pointed out, Much Ado About Murder provides a “whimsically entertaining night.”

event.title: Dashing Through The Snow
event.description:
By Jones/Hope/Wooten / It’s four days before Christmas in the tiny town of Tinsel, Texas, and a colorful parade of eccentric guests arrive at the Snowflake Inn, decking the halls with holiday hilarity. Trina, the harried yet upbeat innkeeper of this B&B, has more than she can handle coping with these nuttier-than-a-fruitcake lodgers. Hoyt and his sister, Donna Jo, make the mistake of trying to end a 30-year feud between their curmudgeonly aunts, with sidesplitting results. Ainsley and Lenora, self-involved actors from a lower-than-low-budget touring production of A Christmas Carol, descend on the inn to fulfill a promise, leaving comedic chaos in their wake. Add to this Yuletide mayhem an ill-advised romantic rendezvous between Mrs. Claus and one of Santa’s elves, a demanding guest who refuses to leave, not to mention a tipsy housekeeper, and it’s clear it will take more than a kiss under the mistletoe to keep Trina’s spirits merry and bright. But a spur-of-the-moment Christmas Eve wedding that brings together the fabulous Futrelle sisters and their best friend takes a surprising and delightful turn that leads to a laugh-’til-your-sides-ache climax, changing all their lives forever.

event.title: Flip My Quarter
event.description:
Seville Quarter’s Flip My Quarter Happy Hour Just Got Even Better!

Every Friday | 6–8 PM | Seville Quarter

Downtown Pensacola’s hottest new Happy Hour is turning up the fun! After an incredible kickoff that packed the house, Seville Quarter is raising the stakes for Flip My Quarter, making it the can’t-miss Friday tradition.

Starting this week, you can flip your way into free drinks with an upgraded lineup, including:
Super Premium Cocktails
House Wine
Domestic Drafts & Bottled Beer

Here’s how it works:
1️⃣ Order one of the featured drinks.
2️⃣ Tell your bartender: “Flip My Quarter.”
3️⃣ Call it right when the Quarter’s in the air → Your drink is FREE!
4️⃣ Miss the call → You pay.

It’s that easy, and that fun. Add in live music, legendary Seville vibes, and the best crowd in town, and you’ve got the perfect way to kick off your weekend.

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.title: Boots, Buckles & Boogie
event.description:
Boots, Buckles & Boogie

Tuesday Country Nights at Seville Quarter

Welcome to Boss Phogg’s Honky-Tonk, where Tuesday nights are made for boots, buckles, and boogie!

event.title: Flip My Quarter
event.description:
Seville Quarter’s Flip My Quarter Happy Hour Just Got Even Better!

Every Friday | 6–8 PM | Seville Quarter

Downtown Pensacola’s hottest new Happy Hour is turning up the fun! After an incredible kickoff that packed the house, Seville Quarter is raising the stakes for Flip My Quarter, making it the can’t-miss Friday tradition.

Starting this week, you can flip your way into free drinks with an upgraded lineup, including:
Super Premium Cocktails
House Wine
Domestic Drafts & Bottled Beer

Here’s how it works:
1️⃣ Order one of the featured drinks.
2️⃣ Tell your bartender: “Flip My Quarter.”
3️⃣ Call it right when the Quarter’s in the air → Your drink is FREE!
4️⃣ Miss the call → You pay.

It’s that easy, and that fun. Add in live music, legendary Seville vibes, and the best crowd in town, and you’ve got the perfect way to kick off your weekend.

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.title: Boots, Buckles & Boogie
event.description:
Boots, Buckles & Boogie

Tuesday Country Nights at Seville Quarter

Welcome to Boss Phogg’s Honky-Tonk, where Tuesday nights are made for boots, buckles, and boogie!

Beginning Tuesday, October 6, Boots, Buckles & Boogie takes over Phineas Phogg’s at Seville Quarter with line dancing, partner dancing, Country Two-Step, Country Swing, and today’s hottest country music.

Dance instructor Dawn Alexander leads line and partner dance lessons from 7–9 p.m. Whether you are learning your first steps or fine-tuning your footwork, Dawn will have you boot-scootin’ with confidence in no time.

After the lessons, Honky-Tonk DJ Miss Janie takes over, playing country-dance favorites all night long on Boss Phogg’s dance floor.

With a true honky-tonk atmosphere andPensacola’s #1 dance floor, Phineas Phogg’s is the perfect place for beginners, experienced dancers, couples, singles, and groups of friends to gather, dance, and show off their moves.

The music will be playing, the crowd will be ready, and Boss Phogg’s dance floor will be calling your name!

 

Boots, Buckles & Boogie
Tuesday Country Nights at Boss Phogg’s

Every Tuesday beginning October 6, 2026
Dance lessons with Dawn Alexander: 7–9 p.m.

event.title: Flip My Quarter
event.description:
Seville Quarter’s Flip My Quarter Happy Hour Just Got Even Better!

Every Friday | 6–8 PM | Seville Quarter

Downtown Pensacola’s hottest new Happy Hour is turning up the fun! After an incredible kickoff that packed the house, Seville Quarter is raising the stakes for Flip My Quarter, making it the can’t-miss Friday tradition.

Starting this week, you can flip your way into free drinks with an upgraded lineup, including:
Super Premium Cocktails
House Wine
Domestic Drafts & Bottled Beer

Here’s how it works:
1️⃣ Order one of the featured drinks.
2️⃣ Tell your bartender: “Flip My Quarter.”
3️⃣ Call it right when the Quarter’s in the air → Your drink is FREE!
4️⃣ Miss the call → You pay.

It’s that easy, and that fun. Add in live music, legendary Seville vibes, and the best crowd in town, and you’ve got the perfect way to kick off your weekend.

Tag your crew. Who’s feeling lucky? Join us this Friday and see if your drinks on the house!

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.title: Flip My Quarter
event.description:
Seville Quarter’s Flip My Quarter Happy Hour Just Got Even Better!

Every Friday | 6–8 PM | Seville Quarter

Downtown Pensacola’s hottest new Happy Hour is turning up the fun! After an incredible kickoff that packed the house, Seville Quarter is raising the stakes for Flip My Quarter, making it the can’t-miss Friday tradition.

Starting this week, you can flip your way into free drinks with an upgraded lineup, including:
Super Premium Cocktails
House Wine
Domestic Drafts & Bottled Beer

Here’s how it works:
1️⃣ Order one of the featured drinks.
2️⃣ Tell your bartender: “Flip My Quarter.”
3️⃣ Call it right when the Quarter’s in the air → Your drink is FREE!
4️⃣ Miss the call → You pay.

It’s that easy, and that fun. Add in live music, legendary Seville vibes, and the best crowd in town, and you’ve got the perfect way to kick off your weekend.

Tag your crew. Who’s feeling lucky? Join us this Friday and see if your drinks on the house!

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

Tuesday Country Nights at Seville Quarter

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

Seville Quarter’s Flip My Quarter Happy Hour Just Got Even Better!

Every Friday | 6–8 PM | Seville Quarter

Downtown Pensacola’s hottest new Happy Hour is turning up the fun! After an incredible kickoff that packed the house, Seville Quarter is raising the stakes for Flip My Quarter, making it the can’t-miss Friday tradition.

Starting this week, you can flip your way into free drinks with an upgraded lineup, including:
Super Premium Cocktails
House Wine
Domestic Drafts & Bottled Beer

Here’s how it works:
1️⃣ Order one of the featured drinks.
2️⃣ Tell your bartender: “Flip My Quarter.”
3️⃣ Call it right when the Quarter’s in the air → Your drink is FREE!
4️⃣ Miss the call → You pay.

It’s that easy, and that fun. Add in live music, legendary Seville vibes, and the best crowd in town, and you’ve got the perfect way to kick off your weekend.

Tag your crew. Who’s feeling lucky? Join us this Friday and see if your drinks on the house!

event.title: Rosie O’Grady’s Dueling Piano Show
event.description:
Every Wednesday, Thursday, Friday & Saturday

You Might Just Be the Star of the Show!

Doors Open at 7:00 PM | Show Starts at 8:00 PM (6:00 PM Every Friday!)

If you’re looking for high-energy entertainment, unforgettable music, and nonstop laughs, Rosie O’Grady’s Dueling Piano Show at Seville Quarter is the place to be in Downtown Pensacola.

Step into the legendary Rosie O’Grady’s Good Time Emporium at 7:00 PM to grab your seat, order a drink, and soak in the lively atmosphere before the show kicks off at 8:00 PM. From the first note to the final encore, this crowd-fueled show delivers Pensacola’s most exciting live entertainment experience.

Featuring four of the South’s top piano players, vocalists, and entertainers, the Dueling Piano Show is a blend of musical talent, comedic timing, and audience interaction. Expect hilarious bits, spontaneous sing-alongs, and your favorite songs by request—plus a few surprises. And who knows? You might just end up in the spotlight!

🍸 Enjoy:
• The Finest Bar & Wait Staff on the Gulf Coast
• Signature cocktails, cold beer, and a full-service bar
• A fun, interactive vibe perfect for date nights, birthday parties, and group celebrations

Come early, stay late, and be part of a Seville Quarter tradition that’s been making memories for decades.

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

Dinner at 5:00 PM | Bingo at 8:00 PM in Apple Annie’s | Free to Play!

Start your week off right with Dinner & Bingo at Seville Quarter!

Come early and grab a bite, Dinner starts at 5:00 PM in Apple Annie’s Courtyard, featuring a full menu of crowd-pleasers: juicy burgers, hot pizzas, wings, fresh Gulf seafood, and more. It’s the perfect way to fuel up before the fun begins!

Then stick around for the wildest Bingo night on the Gulf Coast, Bar Bingo kicks off at 8:00 PM with Seville’s legendary “Good Time Gang” leading the way. It’s free to play, full of laughs, and packed with:

Drink Specials:
• $2.50 Miller Lite Bottles
• $3.50 Bomb Shots
Prizes, Giveaways, & Bar Tabs for Winners!

This ain’t your Grandma’s Bingo (though she’s more than welcome)! Expect hilarious twists, a rowdy crowd, and the kind of good times only Seville Quarter can deliver.
Come for dinner. Stay for the fun. Win big at Bar Bingo!

event.title: Boots, Buckles & Boogie
event.description:
Boots, Buckles & Boogie

Tuesday Country Nights at Seville Quarter

Welcome to Boss Phogg’s Honky-Tonk, where Tuesday nights are made for boots, buckles, and boogie!

Beginning Tuesday, October 6, Boots, Buckles & Boogie takes over Phineas Phogg’s at Seville Quarter with line dancing, partner dancing, Country Two-Step, Country Swing, and today’s hottest country music.

Dance instructor Dawn Alexander leads line and partner dance lessons from 7–9 p.m. Whether you are learning your first steps or fine-tuning your footwork, Dawn will have you boot-scootin’ with confidence in no time.

After the lessons, Honky-Tonk DJ Miss Janie takes over, playing country-dance favorites all night long on Boss Phogg’s dance floor.

With a true honky-tonk atmosphere andPensacola’s #1 dance floor, Phineas Phogg’s is the perfect place for beginners, experienced dancers, couples, singles, and groups of friends to gather, dance, and show off their moves.

The music will be playing, the crowd will be ready, and Boss Phogg’s dance floor will be calling your name!

 

Boots, Buckles & Boogie

Every Tuesday beginning October 6, 2026
Dance lessons with Dawn Alexander: 7–9 p.m.

Learn It Tuesday. Dance It All Weekend.

Run. Refuel. Repeat.
